papers.title: A Causal Schr\"odinger-Newton Theory that Conserves Energy and Momentum
papers.abstract: This paper provides a theoretical justification for using the Causal-Conditional Schr\"odinger-Newton theory (CCSN) as a phenomenological model for classical gravity sourced by quantum matter. In CCSN, the gravitational field is driven not by expectation values in the global quantum state, but by conditional expectation values of the stress-energy tensor evaluated on local states determined by measurement records in the causal past. Because these local states are defined operationally from measurement records, the formulation is independent of any particular interpretation of quantum measurement while leading to unambiguous phenomenological dynamics. We apply this framework to a self-gravitating optomechanical system under continuous measurement and show that the resulting stochastic Schr\"odinger evolution, augmented by a classical gravitational field sourced by local conditional stress-energy expectations, can be made consistent with energy-momentum conservation by introducing a corrector tensor. The corrector restores the conservation law without altering the leading Newtonian predictions of CCSN, contributing only negligible post-Newtonian corrections in current experimental regimes. These results place CCSN on firmer theoretical footing and clarify its role as a viable phenomenological model for ongoing and future tests of classical gravity coupled to quantum matter.
authors: Daisuke Miki, Yanbei Chen, Yiqiu Ma, Yubao Liu, Selim M. Shahriar

papers.title: Physical Realization of the Luczka Model: Inducing Interaction and Entanglement Between Spins
papers.abstract: The Luczka model describes the interaction of spins with a common bosonic environment in the pure-dephasing regime, in which the bosonic modes couple directly to only one spin component. Due to its specific form of interaction, the model is exactly solvable and has been widely used to describe spin decoherence and effective spin-spin interactions mediated by a common bosonic environment. However, to the best of our knowledge, its physical realization and the specific conditions under which such an interaction can be implemented have not yet been addressed. Here, we propose a physical realization of the Luczka spin-environment interaction by coupling the spin system to unidirectionally propagating, polarized electromagnetic radiation. In contrast to the original Luczka model, which allows an arbitrary angular distribution of photon wave vectors, our scheme gives a unidirectional photon flux with retaining a frequency distribution of the photons. As an illustrative application of the proposed realization, we investigate spin-entanglement dynamics for coherent, single-mode thermal, and Ohmic
authors: A. R. Kuzmak

papers.title: In-in formalism & $\mathcal{T}_{C}^{\star}$-product: no contribution from total time derivatives
papers.abstract: In the in-in formalism, total time derivatives are sometimes argued to contribute nontrivially to inflationary correlators at the evaluation point, i.e., at the end of inflation. In this paper, we disprove this claim based on the path integral. After formulating the canonical quantization and the regulated path integral of systems with total time derivatives, we derive the $\mathcal{T}_{C}^{\star}$-ordering, the correct operator ordering on the closed time path. In the $\mathcal{T}_{C}^{\star}$-ordering, the evaluation point, or the turning point of the in-in contour, is merely an intermediate point and is never an endpoint of the generalized path integral contour. As a result, any apparent boundary contributions at the turning point of the forward and backward branches completely cancel out. We demonstrate this cancellation by re-analyzing examples in the literature, with an emphasis on contact terms associated with the $\mathcal{T}_{C}^{\star}$-ordering overlooked previously.
authors: Yohei Ema, Muzi Hong, Ryusuke Jinno, Kyohei Mukaida

papers.title: Exact nonstationary heat-excess statistics in the weakly asymmetric Kipnis--Marchioro--Presutti model
papers.abstract: Exact nonstationary large-deviation statistics remain scarce for interacting many-body systems. Here we employ the macroscopic fluctuation theory (MFT) to determine the complete long-time statistics of heat excess produced by an initially localized heat pulse in the weakly asymmetric Kipnis--Marchioro--Presutti model. We find a remarkable nonlocal canonical transformation which maps the weakly asymmetric MFT problem, including its initial and terminal conditions, onto the symmetric problem, previously solved exactly. The resulting rate function is an explicit nonlinear deformation of its symmetric counterpart. We also extend the solution to heat measured beyond an arbitrary observation point.
authors: Baruch Meerson

papers.title: Beyond Quantum Mechanics: From Nonlinear to Emergent and Solitonic Approaches
papers.abstract: This thesis investigates the role of nonlinearity in approaches beyond standard quantum mechanics, following a path from modifications of quantum dynamics to the possibility of an emergent statistical description. We first examine Weinberg's nonlinear formulation and its implications for the statistical interpretation of quantum states. We then discuss de Broglie-Bohm theory and the Madelung formulation, which provide a framework for comparing guided trajectories with ensemble descriptions involving momentum fluctuations. The Hall-Reginatto exact uncertainty approach identifies the fluctuation energy associated with the quantum potential. We then investigate whether quantum dynamics can emerge from the collective statistics of solitons in a fluctuating background, using a Galilean formulation of the complex sine-Gordon model. Within a weak-noise approximation, we identify a regime in which the statistics of the soliton centres reproduce the Schr{\"o}dinger equation, with an effective action scale determined by the background fluctuations. This correspondence is established for Gaussian ensembles and potentials at most quadratic. These results provide a concrete setting for exploring how quantum dynamics can emerge as a statistical description of underlying nonlinear field dynamics.
authors: Niko Brimi

papers.title: A counterexample to the Ho-Hsieh VQCS saturation conjecture
papers.abstract: We show that there exists a 4-qubit state that can be prepared by a variational quantum-classical simulation (VQCS) circuit ansatz containing 3 layers, but not with 2 layers. This disproves the strong form of a conjecture presented by Ho and Hsieh stating that the expressivity of VQCS on $L$ qubits saturates at $L/2$ layers. The weak form of the conjecture concerning the preparation of the ground state remains open.
authors: Edward Jiang

papers.title: Condensates and Edge Effects in the Generalised Takayasu Model
papers.abstract: Recently, in the 1D Takayasu Mass Model (MM) of diffusion-aggregation with input, large condensates and a novel power law were observed in simulations, and later characterised exactly. We extend these studies to the Takayasu model with generalised input, and provide a relation to translate the distribution function of the MM to any model with a space and time independent injection process. In the 1D Charge Model (CM) of a system of size $L$, where $q=+1$ and $-1$ charge monomers are injected with equal probability at each site in each time step, there is a power law distribution of cluster charge $P(q)\sim |q|^{-5/3}$. This distribution cuts off at $|q|\sim L^{3/2}$ in the steady state for long times $t\gg L^2$ and a large charge condensate forms with a net charge between $-\sqrt{Lt}$ and $\sqrt{Lt}$. A distance dependent distribution function is observed around the charge condensate and near open boundaries, both of which act like an edge in the system, analogous to the observations in the MM. The charge distribution measured at a distance $x$ from the edge transitions from the previously known CM bulk power law $P(q)\sim |q|^{-5/3}$ for small clusters ($|q|< x^{3/2}$), to a novel power law $P(q)\sim |q|^{-7/3}$ for larger clusters ($|q|>x^{3/2}$). In the 1D Pair Injection Model (PIM), where $+1$ and $-1$ charge monomers are injected simultaneously at adjacent sites, the power law distribution $P(q)\sim |q|^{-2}$ cuts off at $|q|\sim L$ in the steady state for long times, and no large growing condensate is formed. We still observe a distance dependent distribution measured from the largest clusters, or an open boundary, with a bulk power law $P(q)\sim |q|^{-2}$ for small clusters ($|q|< x$), and an edge power law $P(q)\sim |q|^{-3}$ for larger clusters ($|q >x$).
authors: Angad Singh

papers.title: On the concentration of the ambiguity function on centered balls
papers.abstract: We show that the Gaussian uniquely maximizes the $L^2$ concentration of the ambiguity function on every centered ball, up to time-frequency shifts and multiplication by a unimodular constant. The proof relies on ideas from quantum information theory.
authors: Fabio Nicola

papers.title: What time is it in Assembly Space? Cronin and Walker's "The Physics of Causation" fails elementary dimensional analysis (Comment on arXiv:2601.00515)
papers.abstract: Cronin and Walker claim that causation is quantified by an ``assembly index'', a count of the steps needed to build an object. Remarkably, they equate ``continuous time (as measured by clocks)'' to a multiple of the index, which is a dimensionless number. Their argument treats one parameter as simultaneously a rate, a time interval, and a pure number, and provides no timescale to convert index to clock time. This dimensional incoherence betrays, at best, an ill-conceived and ill-formed theory, and fatally undermines two central claims. First, the exponential weighting at the heart of what they call the assembly equation can be obtained only by supplying a timescale, which they never do, or by recasting clock time as a dimensionless count of assembly steps. In the latter case, their ``derivation'' trivially reduces to Bernoulli's seventeenth-century compound-interest limit. Second, lacking rates or energy scales, their account cannot predict how quickly, or under what conditions, anything forms, and yet formation ``in finite time'' is their criterion for distinguishing spontaneous from ``selected'' objects. Assembly theory is thus incapable of addressing causation.
authors: Philip Moriarty

papers.title: Superdaisy Resummation in Theories with Broken Gauge Symmetries
papers.abstract: We extend the partial dressing resummation scheme for the finite-temperature effective potential to the gauge and ghost sectors of spontaneously broken gauge theories and apply the resulting framework to the Standard Model. Going beyond the usual high-temperature treatment, we retain the full mass dependence of the thermal self-energies and determine the scalar, gauge-boson and ghost masses self-consistently from a coupled system of gap equations. The solutions show that corrections beyond the leading $\mathcal{O}(T^2)$ approximation are particularly relevant for the gauge-boson thermal masses, while they induce a comparatively small shift in the scalar spectrum for the benchmark studied. The self-consistent gauge-boson dressing in the longitudinal sector reduces the barrier in the finite-temperature Higgs effective potential. Implementing the resummation in the transverse sector removes the barrier and would seem to exclude a first-order phase transition in accordance with lattice results. While such resummation is not quantitatively reliable, due to the transverse excitations becoming strongly coupled, the results showcase the crucial role played by transverse modes in determining the nature of the electroweak phase transition.
authors: Martin M\"unzenberg, Carlos Tamarit

papers.title: Morphogenic necking of surfaces
papers.abstract: Surface morphogenesis occurs across biological scales, from subcellular vesicles and cells to visceral organs, tissue organoids, and whole organisms. Since morphogenesis often involves changes in topology, a natural question is that of appropriate mathematical descriptions that provide an approach to topological transitions of thin surfaces. Here, we suggest a general intrinsic framework coupling morphogen organization to surface geometry. We propose a minimal geometric model in which smoothing competes with morphogen-induced deformation to regulate shape, while loss of this balance can bring a surface toward a topological transition via neck constriction. A simple dynamical model coupling a scalar field to the surface metric reveals two mechanisms: gradient-driven constriction at steep morphogen transitions and curvature-driven constriction near localized morphogen peaks. For frozen morphogen profiles in simple axisymmetric examples, the gradient-driven route gives exact algebraic contraction, while the curvature-driven route gives local exponential contraction.
authors: Farzan Vafa, Puskar Mondal, L. Mahadevan

papers.title: Certifying closed labs in device-independent tests of indefinite causality
papers.abstract: Indefinite causal order allows processes in which the order of events is not predetermined, enabling information-processing advantages unattainable with fixed causal structures. A long-standing open problem is whether such processes can be certified without trusting the devices used to demonstrate them, analogous to device-independent certifications of Bell nonlocality. Causal inequalities offer a route towards this goal, since their violation is intended to rule out all definite causal structures. However, fully device-independent certification of indefinite causal order remains elusive. The difficulty lies in the closed laboratories assumption, which requires each party to interact at most once with systems that mediate communication. Without this assumption, ordinary two-way communication can reproduce causal-inequality violations without involving indefinite causal order. Yet an untrusted device could violate the assumption by interacting with the mediating system more than once, while remaining undetected from input-output statistics alone. We address this loophole by embedding a minimal set of additional experimental components into a certification scheme. These elements probabilistically probe the underlying process, enabling the closed laboratories assumption to be validated directly within the protocol. Our framework provides operationally meaningful minimal-assumption tests of indefinite causal order, clarifying its distinction from nonlocality and paving the way for cryptographic and self-testing applications.
authors: Hannah Seabrook, Fabio Costa, Paul Skrzypczyk, Giulia Rubino

papers.title: Locality from Nonlocality: Symmetry Relocalization and Gauging of Lattice Dirac Fermions
papers.abstract: Spatially nonlocal symmetries need not imply nonlocal gauge dynamics. Nonlocal canonical transformations make certain exact nonlocal compact symmetries of free lattice Dirac fermions onsite while retaining sufficient Hamiltonian locality for gauging. Symmetry relocalization yields exact or emergent gauge locality in 1D, 2D, and 3D, subject to lattice structure, topology, and anomalies. In 1D, a Hamiltonian-preserving transformation exchanges onsite vector and nonlocal spectral axial charges of a half-filled chain, enabling local gauging of each and exposing their mixed anomaly. Bosonization identifies momentum-winding T-duality, with a parity-projected operator flowing to a noninvertible topological defect. A nonperturbative norm-resolvent bound proves emergent dynamical gauge locality at finite chemical potential, while a doubled Chern-insulator parent reveals the duality's bulk origin and superconducting extensions reveal hidden compact symmetries. In 2D, the square $\pi$-flux Majorana model shares the Kitaev honeycomb model's single Dirac fermion and odd Pfaffian parity but supports sharp and exponentially local compact charges, the latter with nontrivial Chern topology. Relocalization retains Schwartz locality for asymptotically local gauging, while AIII/AII parents clarify bulk charge origin and parity-anomaly inflow. Two flavors yield compact $U(2)$, a quaternionic invariant, and asymptotically local non-Abelian gauging. In 3D, an exact mixed vector-axial flux response is derived, while a distinct model supports an exponentially local vector $U(1)$ charge with strong quaternionic topology. A nonlocal map makes the charge and Kramers symmetry onsite while preserving exponential Hamiltonian locality. For a compact $SU(2)$ Weyl doublet, a no-go theorem forbids translation-preserving Gaussian onsite relocalization retaining Weyl content and Hamiltonian locality.
authors: Lei Su

papers.title: The Hidden Simplicity of the Classical Limit
papers.abstract: We study the classical limit of two-to-two massive-scalar amplitudes at all orders of perturbation theory. We compute these amplitudes in the probe limit for several theories: a family of scalar theories, electrodynamics, and $\mathcal{N}=8$ supergravity with half-BPS matter. We show that related multiple-emission classical amplitudes obey a simple factorization derivable from the usual factorization of quantum amplitudes. The classical factorization, which reflects the second-order nature of classical dynamics, holds in more general theories --- including gravity. We further show that both the multiple-emission and the two-to-two classical amplitudes have a simple organization in terms of weighted trees. This allows a recursive computation to all orders in the probe limit. The probe's trajectory emerges as a generating function of trees. The required boundary conditions are given by the Feynman $i \varepsilon$ prescription, leading to a novel worldline Green's function. In our approach, the rich classical dynamics arises from simple combinatorics.
authors: Yilber Fabian Bautista, Stefano De Angelis, David A. Kosower, Donal O'Connell, Matteo Sergola

papers.title: Ground-State Chiral Quantum Clusters
papers.abstract: Quantum time crystals are states of matter that spontaneously break time translation symmetry, extending the notion of crystalline order to time. While their out-of-equilibrium version has been successfully realized by periodic driving, the equilibrium counterpart remains elusive. Here we introduce "ground-state chiral quantum clusters": self-bound many-body ground states supporting a persistent current. We provide a minimal field theory describing these states, and an exact microscopic realization via the attractive anyonic Lieb-Liniger model on a ring. In the latter, the ground-state density-density correlator exhibits the Talbot effect, with a soliton-like profile that periodically disperses and revives while drifting indefinitely along the ring, realizing persistent motion at equilibrium. Possible experimental probes are discussed.
authors: Matteo Massaro, Adolfo del Campo

papers.title: Bootstrapping two-loop $\beta$-functions for bosonic and heterotic strings
papers.abstract: Beyond one loop, $\beta$-functions of non-linear $\sigma$-models are hard to compute directly. We obtain them instead as a gradient flow of the low-energy effective action, whose coupling-space metric is fixed exclusively by symmetry. This gives a two-parameter family of O$(d,d)$-covariant, two-loop $\beta$-functions that covers the bosonic and heterotic string at once. Because only symmetry enters, the method opens a route to higher loops. As an application, we derive the two-loop RG flow of the integrable $\eta$- and $\lambda$-deformations; for the heterotic string, the correction is half of the bosonic one.
authors: Achilleas Gitsis, Falk Hassler

papers.title: Spinal reflected entropy reveals logical magic
papers.abstract: Entanglement and magic are usually regarded as independent quantum resources. Here we connect the two in the toric code, where the stabilizer R\'enyi entropy of the stored logical state, a widely used measure of magic, acquires a direct interpretation in terms of entanglement. We introduce the spinal reflected entropy, defined on a neighborhood of a spine of the underlying surface as the reflected entropy between a disk around the vertex of the spine and bands along its noncontractible loops. It obeys an area law with a topological correction and contains one additional term that carries all the dependence on the stored state. On a torus, this term equals the stabilizer R\'enyi entropy of the stored state plus the logarithm of the ground-state degeneracy. The mechanism is topological. On the surface sewn to its reflected copy, the bands close into tubes, logical Pauli operators become anyon charges threading them, and these charges are distributed as the outcomes of Bell sampling of the stored state. The result extends to surfaces of higher genus and to general two-dimensional topological stabilizer codes on qubits. Logical magic thus becomes a geometrically defined entanglement quantity, one that shallow circuits preserving the code space cannot change.
authors: Zong-Yue Hou, Yuzhen Zhang, Zhi-Cheng Yang, Yingfei Gu

papers.title: A Kerr-black-hole worldline action to $\mathcal{O}(G^5)$
papers.abstract: We establish a worldline action which correctly reproduces Kerr-black-hole dynamics up to fifth order in Newton's constant in a physical post-Minkowskian counting. This encompasses operators up to second order in the Riemann curvature tensor and up to fourth order in the spin tensor. Doing so entails performing the full effective-field-theory computation of the amplitude for a gravitational-wave scattering off of a spinning compact object up to four-loop order, and matching the result to the predictions from linear black hole perturbation theory. Quadratic-in-curvature operators which must be added to match successfully include time-reversal anti-symmetric ones at linear and cubic spin orders, capturing absorption across the black hole horizon, and conservative quadratic-in-spin ones. As an immediate application of our action, we compute the leading-order change in spin magnitude, and reproduce the leading change in mass, for a Kerr black hole in a scattering event with a second compact body, considering a generic orientation of the black hole's spin.
authors: Yilber Fabian Bautista, Mathias Driesse, Kays Haddad, Gustav Uhre Jakobsen

papers.title: Casimir Experiments as Spin-Force Detectors
papers.abstract: Precision Casimir experiments enable highly sensitive probes of short range forces, but have thus far constrained only spin-independent interactions. We show that measurements between reversed polarizations of a magnetically compensated source enable direct searches of axion-mediated monopole-dipole forces. The spin force reverses sign, while the common Casimir, gravitational and electrostatic backgrounds broadly cancel. Compensated sources need no intervening shielding, allowing large probes at micrometer gaps. Casimir experiments could probe the couplings $g_p^e g_s^{N}$ and $g_p^e g_s^{e}$ at $\lambda\sim1-100~\mu{\rm m}$ orders of magnitude beyond existing laboratory searches.
authors: Xiaolin Ma, Volodymyr Takhistov, Hideo Iizuka

papers.title: Free hyperboloidal evolution in 3D: gauge waves and constraint-violating gravitational waves
papers.abstract: Hyperboloidal evolution allows to reach future null infinity within numerical relativity simulations. This work extends the conformal compactification approach with BSSN/Z4 from spherical symmetry to full 3D simulations. This is the first free numerical hyperboloidal evolution in 3D with a common formulation of general relativity. In this first step, gauge waves and constraint-violating gravitational waves perturbing Minkowski spacetime are evolved nonlinearly and show that the implementation is reliable and signals can be successfully extracted at future null infinity.
authors: Alex Va\~n\'o-Vi\~nuales

papers.title: Quantum State Preparation from Nonreversible Markov Chains via Spectral Filtering
papers.abstract: We develop a framework for preparing and transporting coherent quantum samples of nonreversible Markov chains. Our approach uses spectral filtering to construct state-dependent phase operations, which are combined with fixed-point amplitude amplification to transport quantum states along a sequence of related chains. We study two complementary constructions with different oracle requirements and target states. The first uses coherent access to both forward and time-reversed transitions and targets the stationary quantum sample, with a filtering cost governed by a multiplicative-reversibilization gap. The second requires only forward transitions and selects the leading eigenstate of a flat discriminant, which may differ from the stationary quantum sample; we quantify this bias under additional spectral and reversibility-on-average conditions. For the forward-only construction, we implement the spectral filter using generalized quantum signal processing with a single signal qubit, apart from transition registers and oracle workspace. We establish a common transport procedure and derive error and resource bounds that account for spectral properties, overlaps between successive selected states, and the costs of coherent multi-step transition oracles. Up to logarithmic factors, spectral-filter degrees scale inversely with the square roots of the relevant spectral gaps, while transport introduces an additional inverse-square-root dependence on certified lower bounds on squared overlaps between successive selected states. Our results extend existing nonreversible spectral methods to multistage coherent state transport with controlled approximation errors.
authors: Wael Drif

papers.title: Localization in one-dimensional magnetic quasicrystals
papers.abstract: The celebrated Aubry-Andr\'e-Harper model undergoes a metal-insulator transition akin to Anderson localization due to an energetic competition between nearest-neighbor hopping and a quasiperiodic on-site potential. In this work, we consider the problem of a one-dimensional lattice subject to a quasiperiodic external field, where the topology of the underlying graph mediates the competition between insulating and conducting phases. In particular, we present examples for which all dispersive eigenstates are critically localized, as well as models in which they are exponentially localized. We also demonstrate the coexistence of these phenomena with an extensive set of degenerate finitely supported eigenstates forming a flat band. Finally, we construct models with exactly solvable mobility edges arising only from graph structure. Going beyond these single-particle results, we show---using exact-diagonalization calculations of the bosonic dynamics---that, as in the conventional Aubry-Andr\'e-Harper case, on-site interactions drive localized eigenstates toward extendedness. Our results provide a framework for exploring how magnetic interference and interactions jointly constrain transport in quasiperiodic lattices.
authors: Andrew Osborne, Rhine Samajdar, Andrew A. Houck

papers.title: Circulating currents around orbifolded defects
papers.abstract: We investigate holographic monodromy defects with five dimensional orbifold singularities which lift to smooth and supersymmetric ten dimensional geometries. Such geometries have been of recent interest in spindle compactifications and have been interpreted as generalized Gukov-Witten defects. They are constructed by taking an orbifold of previously considered holographic monodromy defects on a space with a conical excess angle, and are not adiabatically connected to the empty anti-de Sitter vacuum. The the orbifold action acts nontrivially both on the five dimensional base as well as the five-sphere. We calculate one-point functions and anomaly coefficients as a function of the monodromies and orbifold data. Surprisingly, we discover that defects exhibit nonzero circulating currents even when all monodromies are turned off, unlike defects adiabatically connected to the vacuum, and therefore correspond to 1/8-BPS excited states. Comparing defects with nontrivial bulk topology we find that the A-type anomaly coefficient is always larger than those with trivial topology, while the B-type coefficient can be either larger or smaller.
authors: Matthew M. Roberts

papers.title: The Schwarzschild-Kerr crossover of high overtone quasinormal modes
papers.abstract: A slowly rotating black hole is close to a nonrotating one, but its highly damped quasinormal spectrum is not. The Schwarzschild approximation holds only up to overtone numbers of order $\chi^{-4/3}$, where $\chi$ is the dimensionless spin. We find that the frequency shift at this scale is a universal function, derived from the wave boundary conditions with an error estimate. It is given by the spectrum of a sextic oscillator, via the correspondence between ordinary differential equations and integrable models. It recovers the Schwarzschild $\log 3$ and organizes the singular Kerr coefficients.
authors: Yasuyuki Hatsuda

papers.title: Refined R\'enyi Entropy from Replica-Geometry Tensor Networks
papers.abstract: Holographic tensor networks are a central route to understanding the mechanism behind the holographic duality, but standard fixed-graph constructions with maximally entangled links face a structural obstacle. Their leading entanglement spectra are flat, so their R\'enyi entropies do not depend on the replica index. This is in sharp contrast with holographic conformal field theories, where a tensionful cosmic brane makes the refined R\'enyi entropy $n$-dependent. Capturing this replica dependence is therefore an important test of tensor-network descriptions of holographic entanglement. We construct an explicit family of replica-dependent geodesic graphs that reproduces this behavior while keeping the links maximally entangled. For each replica index $n$, geodesics are emitted from the replicated boundary with the same local, isotropic intersection measure. They perfectly tessellate the selected replica geometry, so the $n$-dependence of their intersection counts comes from the geometry. Tensor-network models on these graphs reproduce the cosmic-brane prescription for refined R\'enyi entropy by counting crossing threads. Their cross-copy endpoint density also agrees, in CFT$_2$, with a boundary reconstruction within the additive linear combination proposal, providing a check beyond the total entropy. In higher dimensions, we further obtain an analytic large-separation decay law for this density.
authors: Qiang Wen, Haocheng Zhong, Yiwei Zhong

papers.title: Quantum black hole evaporation from thin shell collapse: a complete effective picture
papers.abstract: Quantum gravity is expected to play a central role in resolving classical singularities and providing a complete, predictive spacetime picture. In this paper, we develop an effective model inspired by loop quantum gravity that aims to fulfill this expectation, providing a unified description of thin shell collapse, black hole formation, evaporation, and remnant dynamics. The framework exhibits general validity, holding across different effective equations of motion, matter sources, and evaporation laws. Specifically, we incorporate backreaction within a quasi-static approximation, modeling the radiation as null dust and matching the ingoing and outgoing fluxes across an evaporation surface using the Darmois-Israel junction conditions. For an evaporation law governed by the Stefan-Boltzmann law, we find that the final stage of evaporation yields an extremal black hole extending into a new asymptotic region, featuring both event and Cauchy horizons. Conversely, under the Schwinger approach, no event or Cauchy horizons form, instead, a temporary dynamical trapped region emerges, and the resulting spacetime remains globally hyperbolic. Under this variant, our model predicts a horizonless null remnant escaping to future null infinity.
authors: Micha{\l} Bobula, Francesco Fazzini

papers.title: A Constraint-Preserving Preconditioned Quantum Solver for Heterogeneous Brinkman Flo
papers.abstract: Quantum amplitude estimation can reduce the number of evaluations needed to estimate an average, but its advantage in PDE uncertainty quantification depends on the cost of each coherent solve. We study this problem for incompressible Brinkman flow through a porous material with spatially varying drag. We first express the velocity in divergence-free coordinates using a polar Riesz map, obtaining a positive-definite system that preserves incompressibility in the exact formulation. We then introduce a Sobolev--Riesz preconditioner and prove that the resulting condition number is bounded by $\alpha_{\max}/\alpha_{\min}$, independently of the grid resolution. We construct block encodings and reversible-arithmetic circuits for this formulation and show how to estimate the mean kinetic energy without reconstructing the full velocity field. By accounting for both sampling and solver costs, we establish conditions under which the method has a gate-complexity advantage over single-level classical grid-resolving solvers. Numerical experiments verify the conditioning bound and the accuracy of the circuit components at the tested sizes. The complexity advantage is conditional on the stated input and discretization assumptions; no quantum-hardware runtime advantage is demonstrated.
authors: Shreya Savadatti, Franz Franchetti

papers.title: Elliptic spin Ruijsenaars--Schneider model via the Poisson reduction of the affine Heisenberg double
papers.abstract: We construct the Hamiltonian structure of the elliptic spin Ruijsenaars--Schneider model with dynamical inhomogeneities by Poisson reduction of the affine Heisenberg double extended by an affine oscillator manifold. This construction extends the Heisenberg double approach to spin Ruijsenaars--Schneider models from the hyperbolic to the elliptic case. We solve the moment map constraint and derive the Poisson algebras of the invariant Lax operator and spin variables. A realization with finitely many degrees of freedom is obtained by evaluating and localizing the invariant oscillators at distinct points of the affine parameter. Consistency requires these points to be dynamical so that their nontrivial Poisson brackets with the spin variables cancel derivative terms that would otherwise obstruct closure of the Poisson bracket on finitely many degrees of freedom. The resulting Poisson brackets and Hamiltonian coincide with those recently obtained from the elliptic Coulomb branch of the necklace quiver. Our construction thus provides an independent derivation of this Hamiltonian structure and establishes a direct link between Poisson reductions and Coulomb branches.
authors: Gleb Arutyunov, Lukas Hardi, Davide Polvara

papers.title: Flat Space Entanglement from Wedge Holography
papers.abstract: We study holographic entanglement entropy in three-dimensional flat space by combining wedge holography with a controlled flat limit of AdS end-of-the-world branes. The limit takes a wedge of AdS$_4$ bounded by two AdS$_3$ branes to a Randall-Sundrum-like configuration of two flat branes, and the entanglement entropy of an interval in the two-dimensional corner CFT becomes that of an interval at null infinity of the branes. The result has the functional form of the entanglement entropy of a two-dimensional Carrollian CFT, the proposed holographic dual of gravity in asymptotically flat three-dimensional spacetimes. However, the inferred central charges yield $c_M=0$ and $c_L\to\infty$ in the flat limit. Adding a gravitational Chern-Simons term produces a $c_M$-like contribution, but we still find $c_L\to\infty$ and $c_M\to0$ in this limit. Moreover, the corresponding extremal surfaces do not approach the swing surfaces proposed by Song and collaborators. Instead, they collapse onto null rays along null infinity. We argue that both features are generic for flat limits of AdS/CFT. They follow from entanglement entropy being a property of the domain of dependence and from the equality of causal and entanglement wedges for intervals in the vacuum.
authors: Robert C. Myers, Bruno Sivilotti

papers.title: A spin chain as a deformed conformal field theory: an ODE/IM approach
papers.abstract: The ODE/IM correspondence relates ordinary differential equations to integrable quantum field theories in the continuum. We ask whether it extends to integrable spin chains of finite length $N$. We analyse the twisted XXZ chain at a special anisotropy and twist, focusing on states in its Lee--Yang scaling sector. Their finite-size corrections are expected to come from the Lee--Yang conformal field theory deformed by irrelevant operators, and with the help of the ODE/IM correspondence we make this deformation explicit for the energy and the local conserved charges. Near each of the two edges of the distribution of the Bethe roots, the chain behaves as one chirality of the Lee--Yang theory in a generalised Gibbs ensemble, whose chemical potentials depend on $N$. The ODE/IM correspondence describes each of these ensembles by a cubic oscillator, whose coefficients we determine as series in $1/N$. The two chiralities are not independent: finite-size effects couple them, so that the charges of each shift the chemical potentials of the other. This turns out to be a generalised $T\bar T$-type interaction. Solving this coupling self-consistently, we obtain the energy and the local conserved charges of the chain as series in $1/N$, with no free parameters. We verify these series against the Bethe ansatz, for the ground state and for an excited state.
authors: Sujay K. Ashok, Nicol\`o Primi, Roberto Tateo

papers.title: Topological Phase Transition of $ F_{\alpha }{}^{\gamma } F^{\alpha \beta } F_{\beta }{}^{\eta } \ F^{\lambda \mu } R_{\gamma \eta \lambda \mu } $ AdS Black Holes
papers.abstract: We investigate the thermodynamic criticality and topological properties of four-dimensional charged anti-de Sitter black holes in the presence of a nonminimal electromagnetic-curvature interaction of the form \(F_{\alpha}{}^{\gamma}F^{\alpha\beta}F_{\beta}{}^{\eta}F^{\lambda\mu}R_{\gamma\eta\lambda\mu}\). Treating the coupling perturbatively to first order, we construct the corrected black hole solutions and derive their thermodynamic quantities in the extended phase space. Conventional critical behavior is examined through the criticality conditions for the Hawking temperature in both canonical and grand canonical ensembles. We then use thermodynamic topology to investigate the global structure of equilibrium configurations and its dependence on the thermodynamic parameters. In the canonical ensemble, two distinct regimes emerge: a noncritical region characterized by a total winding number \(W=+1\), and a critical region with \(W=0\). In the grand canonical ensemble, three distinct regimes are identified according to the electric potential. Interestingly, the low- and intermediate-potential regions share the same topological number, \(W=+1\), although conventional critical points occur only in the intermediate-potential region. The high-potential region, by contrast, is characterized by \(W=0\) and exhibits no conventional critical behavior. Our findings show that thermodynamic topology provides a global characterization of equilibrium configurations that complements conventional temperature-based criticality analysis, and that the global winding number alone does not uniquely determine the existence of conventional critical points.
authors: Mehdi Sadeghi, Faramarz Rahmani

papers.title: Quantum Control Under Control-Dependent Decoherence
papers.abstract: Decoherence, which arises from the interaction of a quantum system with a typically much larger thermal environment, or bath, poses major challenges to the controllability of quantum systems. The dynamics of such open quantum systems is often represented by Markovian quantum master equations of the Lindblad or Redfield type. These equations describe the dynamics of the open system with a sum of coherent (Hamiltonian) and decoherent (dissipative) contributions. It is often assumed that coherent controls only impact the coherent contribution, while the decoherent contribution is taken to be time- and control-independent. However, the decoherent contribution must also be control-dependent if coupling to a thermal bath is to relax the system to a Gibbs state at thermal equilibrium, which is given in terms of the system's Hamiltonian. In this paper, we investigate the effect of accounting for control-dependent decoherence on coherent control protocols. To this end, we examine the effect of accounting for control-dependent decoherence on the controllability of an open quantum system in the case of a two-level system coupled to a thermal bath. We show that coherent controls wield greater influence on the dynamics of the system than predicted by a Lindblad-type equation that models decoherence as time- and control-independent.
authors: Cyril Morluyan Cordor, Anthony M. Bloch, Eitan Geva

papers.title: Dynamical phase transition in Brownian motion via sharp large deviations
papers.abstract: We prove a dynamical phase transition in Brownian motion with drift, a phenomenon recently predicted in the physics literature. Specifically, when a Brownian motion with drift on a long time interval is conditioned on an upper large deviation event for the (normalized) occupation measure of the interval [-1,1], in the spirit of the Gibbs conditioning principle, a phase transition occurs. If one conditions on a large deviation event in the far upper tail, the conditioned process follows the Langevin diffusion suggested by the Donsker-Varadhan variational formula for additive functionals. In contrast, if one conditions on a large deviation event in the near upper tail, the conditioned process follows a different Langevin diffusion on a fraction of the time interval and subsequently behaves like the unconditioned process. We establish this phase transition via a new sharp large deviation result for the occupation measure, which is of independent interest. We also provide further corollaries of this result and discuss generalizations to other Markov processes and additive functionals.
authors: Benjamin Budway, Makiko Sasada, Mykhaylo Shkolnikov

papers.title: The Relaxation of Quantum Near-Extremal Black Holes. (I) Microcanonical States, Pruning of Quasinormal Modes, and the Aretakis Instability
papers.abstract: The late-time relaxation of a near-extremal black hole is classically governed by an infinite tower of purely damped quasinormal modes. This poses a puzzle: the higher overtones decay at rates much larger than the energy $E$ of the black hole above extremality, so they would need black hole states below the extremal mass. We resolve it by including the quantum fluctuations that become large when $E$ falls below a scale $E_b$. We compute the retarded Green's function of a probe of conformal dimension $\Delta$ in a black hole of fixed energy, and find that each classical mode splits into a pair of poles with real parts set by $E_b$. The perturbed black hole decays as an unstable quantum system, and a pair is a resonance, i.e., a quasinormal mode, only if its energy lies within the accessible black hole spectrum. This prunes the tower to finitely many modes, all damped faster than $\Delta^2E_b$, and below $E=\Delta^2E_b/2$ none is left. For generic $\Delta$, the response of the black hole decays first as $t^{-2\Delta}$ and finally as $t^{-3/2}$, with an exponential stage in between if $E\gg\Delta^2E_b$. The same quantum effects bear on the Aretakis instability of extremal black holes, in which transverse derivatives of a perturbation grow without bound on the horizon. Like the tower of modes, it originates in the scale invariance of the classical throat, which the quantum fluctuations break. The $t^{-2\Delta}$ decay, which is the boundary counterpart of the Aretakis growth, ends by $t\sim1/E_b$, when the throat ceases to be classical, and by then horizon derivatives have grown only to a finite value. Their unbounded growth is an artifact of taking the semiclassical limit before the late-time one, two limits that in quantum mechanics do not commute.
authors: Roberto Emparan, Sameer Murthy, Stefano Trezzi

papers.title: Long-range effective interactions in a rectangular tight-binding lattice within the semiclassical approximation
papers.abstract: We extend the semiclassical formalism of Dunlap--Kenkre (1986) and of Mamani et al. (2017) to obtain the effective Hamiltonian of a rectangular tight-binding lattice with interactions to all neighbors, in the presence of a rapidly oscillating field $\mathbf f(\omega t)$ and a static potential $V(x,y)$, both arbitrary, by means of: a canonical transformation, the semiclassical approximation and the Kapitza-type time-averaging techniques (Mamani 2017). At zeroth order in $1/\omega$, a field with even symmetry reparameterizes the hopping elements through factors in terms of Bessel functions. At order $1/\omega^2$, the induced hopping elements arise from the coupling between the oscillating field and the curvature of the static potential (its 2nd derivative). For fields $\mathbf f(\omega t)$ with odd symmetry, in addition to renormalizing the interactions, an effective band shift appears. For the two-dimensional lattice, we obtain the generalization of the exact dynamic localization condition of Dignam et al. (2002) and Domachuk et al. (2002), and we show that the resulting band-collapse is in general anisotropic --axial interactions are suppressed but some diagonal interactions persist--, so that exact dynamic localization in the stroboscopic sense is guaranteed only when the band-collapse is complete for all neighbors. Finally, we numerically identify an effective-duplication scenario for the rectangular lattice, associated with approximate solutions of a Pythagorean-type relation among zeros of the zeroth-order Bessel function.
authors: Evaristo Mamani, Diego Sanjines

papers.title: Higher-symmetry selection rules for second- and third-harmonic radiation in the Bullough-Dodd model
papers.abstract: We investigate nonlinear excitations of the discrete shape mode about a static complex soliton of the integrable Bullough-Dodd model. Extending the linear stability analysis to third order in the excitation amplitude, we construct explicit spatially localised corrections to the shape-mode oscillation and determine its nonlinear frequency shift using the Poincar\'e-Lindstedt method. Although both the second and third harmonics lie inside the continuous spectrum of the linearised fluctuation operator, the corresponding inhomogeneous equations admit exact localised particular solutions. We demonstrate that the nonlinear sources have vanishing on-shell overlaps with the scattering states at both harmonic frequencies, suppressing the corresponding radiative responses. We further investigate the role of integrability and show how a higher commuting symmetry of the Bullough-Dodd equation provides a perturbative selection-rule interpretation of these cancellations. Our results illustrate how higher integrable symmetries can constrain nonlinear resonances that are otherwise permitted by the linear spectrum.
authors: Andreas Fring

papers.title: Blueprint for DOE Quantum Supercomputing
papers.abstract: Quantum computing stands at the threshold of a transformative decade, where the field will evolve from small-scale demonstrations toward practical scientific computing at scale. This Blueprint identifies fault-tolerant quantum computers (FTQCs) as a viable, scalable, and broadly applicable path to achieving "quantum scientific utility." It outlines a strategy to prepare the US Department of Energy (DOE) for FTQCs and their integration into the US national scientific computing infrastructure. Its purpose is to identify the steps, milestones, and research directions necessary for DOE to enable initial deployment of FTQCs in 2028 as a scientific tool for the nation and mature this capability into the 2030s. Given recent demonstrations of logical operations on error-corrected logical qubits and the advancement of commercial hardware roadmaps, DOE should begin preparations for large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computing deployment for DOE science missions. This Blueprint proposes that DOE focus on (1) deploying first-generation scientifically relevant quantum computers with at least 100 logical qubits and performing at least 10,000 to 100,000 hard logical operations in scientifically relevant calculations; (2) developing essential FTQC programming competencies, system software, and facility readiness; and (3) investing in cutting-edge focused R&D that fosters breakthroughs in scientific applications, algorithms, and logical architectures needed to accelerate the advent of scientific utility. This effort will position DOE to transition to larger systems: production-scale quantum computers that comprise 1,000 to 10,000 logical qubits, perform 1 to 10 billion hard logical operations, and execute scientifically useful computations at scale. The Blueprint calls for transformative R&D and collective action to accelerate the advent of scientific quantum utility and bring it within reach by 2028.
authors: Ryan Bennink, Robin Blume-Kohout, Salman Habib, Andrew Landahl, Hai Ah Nam, Laura Schulz, Mallikarjun Shankar, Nicholas Wright

papers.title: Exact Scalar and Fermionic Propagators in a Uniform Electric Background
papers.abstract: By implementing an analytical hybrid framework that combines the Ritus eigenfunction technique with Schwinger's proper-time formalism, we construct exact propagators for charged scalar and fermionic fields in a constant, homogeneous, external electric field in four-dimensional Euclidean space. A central advantage of this approach is that the resulting propagators retain a four-dimensional momentum representation after the spectral summation, connecting the structure of the Ritus basis with the operator formulation of the proper-time method, without requiring the full traditional derivation of Schwinger's approach and the coordinate restrictions originally associated with the Ritus method for fermions. The translationally non-invariant component emerging after the Laguerre-polynomial summation is isolated through a suitable change of variables, yielding translationally invariant kernels and maintaining the background field strength unchanged. As a consistency check, we successfully rederive Schwinger's seminal expression for the fermionic pair production rate.
authors: Emerson B. S. Corr\^ea

papers.title: Eigenvalue-based computation of Richardson pairing spectra and finite-size thermodynamics
papers.abstract: We present a numerical workflow for the reduced BCS Richardson model, combining the eigenvalue-based Bethe equations, Baxter-polynomial reconstruction, and complex root finding. Newton-Raphson iteration solves the nonlinear equations for the eigenvalue-based variables; a linear system yields the polynomial coefficients, and Laguerre iteration with polynomial deflation extracts the rapidities. We apply the procedure to equally spaced, quadratic, and hydrogen-like non-degenerate single-particle spectra as the pairing strength varies. For finite systems, we calculate canonical observables from the complete seniority-zero spectrum and check benchmark spectra against exact diagonalization. In an eight-level, four-pair system with a hydrogen-like spectrum, the heat capacity has two maxima at weak coupling. With increasing coupling, the low-temperature maximum shifts upward and the high-temperature maximum downward; the latter ceases to be a distinct local maximum near $g\simeq0.03515$ in the units used. The equally spaced benchmark instead has a single dominant maximum over the coupling interval displayed for that spectrum. This comparison illustrates how single-particle level spacings can shape finite-size thermal response. The C++ code is publicly available; numerical instabilities remain possible near ill-conditioned configurations and at larger sizes.
authors: Grzegorz Biskowski, Marcin R. Piatek, Franco Ferrari

papers.title: All-electronic geometric phase gate on Doppler-cooled trapped ions using an axial mode
papers.abstract: We report the experimental demonstration of a high-fidelity oscillating magnetic gradient entangling gate on the axial stretch mode of a two-ion crystal in a micro-fabricated surface Paul trap, therefore allowing for mixed-species sympathetic cooling. With only Doppler-cooled $^{171}$Yb$^+$ ions at $\bar{n}$ = 50(5), we achieve Bell-state fidelities far above the relevant fault-tolerant threshold, simplifying transport protocols within a shuttling-based-architecture. The control fields consist only of an oscillating current applied to submerged integrated wires emitting a B-field gradient near-resonant with the axial mode, and resonant microwave pulses at the qubit frequency constituting very low gate calibration overheads. We also demonstrate an adiabatic elimination of spin-motion entanglement (AESE) version of the gate, showcasing significant robustness.
authors: P. Rahimi, C. Knapp, P. Zantis, T. Maddock, S. J. Hile, J. Randall, M. Siegele-Brown, S. Weidt, W. K. Hensinger

papers.title: Radiation from periods: Bremsstrahlung functions, wound loops, latitudes and integral constraints in ABJM
papers.abstract: The Bremsstrahlung functions of the 1/2BPS and 1/6BPS Wilson lines of ABJM theory measure their response to small deformations. We show that a single geometric object, the spectral curve of the localisation matrix model, captures both of them in closed form, together with the planar wound and latitude Wilson loops at any complex winding and framing. The fermionic function turns out to be a period of the second kind: a single hypergeometric function, which solves a second-order differential equation and is quasimodular. The bosonic one is not a period but a ratio of periods. At every coupling it is the smaller of the two, so radiation grows along the defect flow from the bosonic to the fermionic line. The key role is played by a new observable, the winding velocity, which turns out to be the 't Hooft coupling shifted by four times the fermionic function. It is at the same time the winding derivative of the wound loop and the curvature of the latitude, and the curve captures it in both incarnations through its logarithmic periods and through its periods with two charges. It is also a datum of the defect conformal field theory on the 1/2BPS line, since it fixes a new integrated four-point function of the tilt operators. All results extend to ABJ theory when the ranks of the gauge groups are not equal.
authors: Michelangelo Preti

papers.title: The other side of the saturation coin: an experiment to perform saturation of fluorescence spectroscopy in undergraduate laboratories
papers.abstract: This article presents an experimental study of saturation and hyperfine pumping effects observed in fluorescence spectra when two counter-propagating beams of light interact with an atomic vapor sample. The experiment focuses on the D2 transition of atomic 87Rb by measuring changes in fluorescence emission as a room-temperature cell is exposed to two counter propagating laser beams of nearly equal intensity. The setup is comparable in complexity to saturated absorption spectroscopy experiments commonly conducted in many undergraduate laboratories but offers the advantage of a complementary view of the atom-light interaction not often found in educational laboratories. The basic theory that is needed to interpret the spectra is also presented. First, an analysis of the timescales involved in these experiments is used to identify and discriminate between different physical processes that take place during the spectroscopic measurements, thus establishing the validity of a simple model based on Einstein's population equations. The solution of these equations is then used to calculate population surfaces that illustrate velocity-selection effects, providing an intuitive explanation of the origin of crossover and atomic resonances and the distinction between them. Both the experimental and theoretical components of this work are aimed at providing students with a thorough understanding of the interaction between electromagnetic radiation and an atomic vapor. Students with prior knowledge of laser optics, basic analog electronics, systems of coupled algebraic equations, introductory quantum mechanics, and basic atomic and statistical physics will be particularly well positioned to benefit from this presentation.
authors: G. Quiroz-S\'anchez, L. M. Hoyos-Campo, J. Flores-Mijangos, F. Ram\'irez-Mart\'inez, J. Jim\'enez-Mier

papers.title: New relations of tree-level string amplitudes from the massless prescription
papers.abstract: We discover new relations between the string corrections to $(m+1)$-point field-theory amplitudes and $m$-point string amplitudes at tree level from the massless prescription of vertex operators.
authors: Chen Huang, Yi-Xiao Tao

papers.title: Absence of $\sigma$-criticality in Short-Range Spin Glasses
papers.abstract: The stability of ground states in the Edwards-Anderson Ising spin glass in dimensions two and higher against perturbations of a single coupling can be quantified through the ``flexibility'' of that coupling in a particular ground state. The property of $\sigma$-criticality is one in which varying a single coupling can alter the flexibilities of a (strictly) positive density of couplings in an infinite system, and its presence provides a sufficient condition for the presence of multiple ground state pairs. In a previous paper it was shown for the EA spin glass that $\sigma$-criticality of the first kind, in which the critical droplet of a bond has a positive-density interface with the ground state, was ruled out in any dimension. The remaining possibility, called $\sigma$-criticality of the second kind, is one in which a bond lies in the critical droplet boundaries of a positive density of other bonds. We show here that this kind of $\sigma$-criticality is also absent, ruling out altogether the presence of $\sigma$-criticality in the EA spin glass. While this doesn't resolve the question of multiplicity of ground state pairs, it removes a sufficient condition for its presence. We then propose a rigorous necessary condition for ground state pair multiplicity.
authors: C. M. Newman, D. L. Stein

papers.title: How Small Can a Single Shor Run Be? Limits and Constructions for secp256k1
papers.abstract: Most resource estimates for breaking secp256k1 with Shor's algorithm describe one long run per attempt, and the spacetime volume of that run, its peak number of logical qubits times its Toffoli count, sets its logical-error budget. Eker{\aa}'s tradeoff shrinks each run by using more runs, but how far it can shrink the largest run, and at what circuit cost, has not been determined. We minimize the volume of the largest run while every key is recovered with probability at least 0.99, within ten times the total volume of three runs of H\"aner et al.\ and $2^{40}$ classical operations. We prove that a linear run fixed in advance, which starts its group register at a point and discards its label, reveals at most $\log_2(1+(|S|-1)/r)$ bits about a uniform key, where $|S|$ counts its exponent values and $r$ is the group order. With generic post-processing and the baseline's window costs, splitting alone then shrinks the largest run at most 1.86 times within the budget. To gain more, we make each exponent bit cheaper with windows that share one table point among exponent values related by six symmetries of the curve, on a point-addition core borrowed from the ECDSA.Fail leaderboard. One random scalar and one random start per run give every approximate addition uniform operands, and a bound on each run's outcomes certifies, for every key, a decoder that discards flagged runs. We count every Toffoli gate and every qubit of every run, and each configuration solved all 563 of its pre-registered simulated trials on secp256k1. The best one shrinks the largest run 3.87 times at 8.79 times the baseline's total volume, against 2.81 times for Eker{\aa}'s tradeoff on the same core, and its run is at least 2.6 times smaller than every design of Initio Intelligence.
authors: Yicheng Guang, Yuliang Xiong, Yueqi Chen, Xun Gao

papers.title: All the Positive Energy Correlators
papers.abstract: We develop a framework to systematically obtain the full set of positivity bounds on multi-point energy correlators for sources of arbitrary spin. The constraints are organized in a family of positive operators $\mathscr{E}^{(N,k)}$, with $k=0,\ldots,\lfloor N/2\rfloor$. Our approach provides outer bounds, which exclude correlators that violate the positivity of $\mathscr{E}^{(N,k)}$, and inner bounds, obtained by constructing ensembles of consistent collider events via linear programming. Both methods converge to each other as numerical precision increases. This approach, in particular, characterizes the allowed higher-point correlators once lower-point correlators are determined. We illustrate this through several examples, including bounds on multipoles of the three-point energy correlator in QCD derived from measurements of one- and two-point correlators at LEP.
authors: Lorenzo Ricci, Marc Riembau, Minho Son

papers.title: Neural Decoding of Logical Clifford Circuits with Transversal Gates
papers.abstract: On neutral-atom and trapped-ion machines, a transversal gate needs only one syndrome round, so a logical gate takes up to d times less time than with lattice surgery. However, transversal gates make decoding harder, because a transversal CNOT copies errors between two blocks of physical qubits, so a decoder must read all blocks of a circuit together. Algorithmic decoders for such circuits gain accuracy at the cost of speed. Neural decoders ease this trade-off, but they must infer from data where errors go across each gate and how logical outcomes propagate through the circuit, although both are known exactly. In this work, we present Duet, a neural decoder for logical Clifford circuits with transversal gates that builds in this known information and learns only which errors occurred. Duet leverages three insights. First, each transversal gate moves an error to a fixed place, so the network exchanges features only between the sites that a gate connects. Second, a logical outcome propagates through Clifford gates exactly and linearly, so the network predicts only the flips that the errors of each layer cause and combines the layers by a soft XOR. Third, every circuit is built from the same few gates, so the network takes the gates of each layer as input and one network per code distance decodes circuits of different sizes and depths. We pair Duet with the search decoder Tesseract, which re-decodes the few shots on which the network is least confident. On general circuits with 2 to 4 blocks and up to 16 layers, Duet alone is already more accurate than matching at every distance, and with Tesseract it fails 44 times less often than LoMatching at distance 9. On the random circuits of the Lukin group, it fails 0.299 times as often as their neural decoder at distance 7. The composition stays fast and takes 2.4 to 121.7 {\mu}s per layer, less than their network takes per gate at every distance.
authors: Yicheng Guang, Yuliang Xiong, Xun Gao, Yueqi Chen

papers.title: From Growth Inhibition to Fluctuations: Testing an Ising Model of Bacterial Responses to Antibiotics
papers.abstract: Complex networks of biochemical reactions have been proposed to exhibit emergent cooperativity that can be described by an effective Ising model, with a small number of parameters encoding collective interactions. Here this mapping is experimentally tested using the response of three bacterial species to a range of antibiotics acting on different cellular targets. The Ising description is compared to the conventional Hill model, examining both the mean growth-rate response and, importantly, its population growth-rate heterogeneity (PGRH). While both models describe the mean growth-rate dependence on antibiotic concentration comparably well, we find that the Ising model provides a markedly better description of PGRH, offering an additional and more stringent test of the collective description. The fitted Ising interaction strength is systematically related to the Hill exponent and increases with the functional distance of the antibiotic target from the protein-production machinery. These results provide experimental support for describing complex biochemical reaction networks through effective cooperative Ising interactions, and suggest that the collective response of bacterial growth to antibiotics reflects the organization of the underlying metabolic network.
authors: Pietro Cicuta, Morten Kals, Nir S. Gov

papers.title: The Eigenfunction Method to Calculate the Klein--Gordon Propa-gator in an Inhomogeneous Magnetic Field
papers.abstract: In this paper, we use the Eigenfunction method (Ritus' method) to calculate the Klein--Gordon propagator under an external magnetic field with an exponential damping factor $b$, in a four-dimensional Euclidean space. We write the propagator of scalar field in terms of plane waves and Laguerre polynomials. Also the eigenvalues associated to differential operator show the quantization in the $\mathrm{xy}$-plane through the Landau levels. We apply the calculated propagator to the mass parameter of an interacting boson system under an exponentially decaying magnetic field.
authors: Emerson B. S. Corr\^{e}, Mateus G. Lima, Suellen. C. Q. Arruda

papers.title: Adaptive ghost Gutzwiller dynamics of Hubbard model quenches across coupling strengths over extended times
papers.abstract: Following the real-time dynamics of correlated electrons to extended times, at all interaction strengths, remains an open challenge. We address it with an adaptive time-dependent ghost Gutzwiller approximation (td-gGA). The method extends the Gutzwiller approximation by auxiliary ghost orbitals. It adds more of them whenever the correlations that build up during the dynamics exceed a threshold. This is computationally far more efficient than keeping their number fixed. As a demonstration we take the interaction quench of the half-filled Hubbard model on the Bethe lattice. For this paradigmatic problem, numerically exact nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) serves as the reference. A previous td-gGA study with a fixed set of 6 ghost orbitals per spin largely reproduced the available DMFT data. It lacked, however, an error estimate that would support predictions beyond them. With up to 16 ghost orbitals per spin, adaptive td-gGA agrees with DMFT wherever DMFT data are available, from the weak-coupling prethermal regime to the strong-coupling collapse-and-revival regime. At strong coupling it remains converged up to three and a half times as long as the DMFT data. Near the crossover between the two regimes, the system relaxes to thermal values that agree with DMFT. Resolving the dynamics in the number of ghost orbitals shows how the sharp dynamical transition of the Gutzwiller approximation turns into this smooth crossover. In the extended time window at strong coupling, we observe that the oscillation frequency is renormalized as predicted by our second-order strong-coupling expansion. With its built-in error estimate, adaptive td-gGA offers a systematically improvable route to the extended-time dynamics of driven and multi-orbital correlated systems, especially when combined with tensor-network or quantum solvers for the embedding problem.
authors: Yong-Xin Yao

papers.title: Scaling Limits of Time-averaged Distributions for Symmetric Quantum Walks on Hypercubes
papers.abstract: We study continuous-time and discrete-time quantum walks on the hypercube $\{0,1\}^d$ associated with symmetric random walks, that is, random walks whose transition probabilities depend only on the Hamming distance, using the Hamming scheme and Krawtchouk polynomials. For continuous-time walks, we show that the time-averaged distribution of the Hamming distance is a discrete arcsine law whenever the eigenvalues are distinct. For discrete-time walks, exact formulas for the time-averaged distribution are known as combinatorial sums or as mixtures involving Krawtchouk polynomials, but their scaling limits as $d\to\infty$ (time average first) have not been specified. We obtain them explicitly for three random walks: the simple random walk (an arcsine law), the random walk with binomial weights (an equal mixture of arcsine laws with different supports), and the independent random walk (atoms of mass $1/2$ at $0$ and at $1/2$). Comparing with the continuous-time limits, the two models agree for the simple random walk but differ for the other two, so the correspondence between them is not universal.
authors: Yusuke Ide, Norio Konno, Shuhei Mano

papers.title: The Matrix in Pieces: Complete BFSS Scattering at Finite Rank
papers.abstract: As two matrix blocks separate in Banks-Fischler-Shenker-Susskind matrix quantum mechanics, the modes connecting them develop a growing excitation gap. Supersymmetry cancels their leading vacuum energy, so blocks in internal bound states can scatter as composite particles. We prove that these particle channels are asymptotically complete for the physical relative Hamiltonian at each fixed finite rank $N\ge 2$. Because a block can itself break up as its center moves away from the others, the proof must control motion on both scales. Inverse powers of the matrix radius control derivatives along internal flat directions, while the growing gap suppresses excitations between blocks. Propagation estimates then allow us to resolve successive breakups by induction on the block rank. The incoming and outgoing wave operators each have range equal to the absolutely continuous subspace, and the singular-continuous subspace vanishes. The scattering operator is thus unitary when each constituent can occupy any of its internal bound states. For a normalized incoming state of zero-energy constituents, the outgoing probability missing from the zero-energy channels equals the inclusive probability of producing at least one constituent with positive internal energy.
authors: Mai Qi

papers.title: Second-order localization and intersecting O6-planes in scale-separated AdS vacua
papers.abstract: We construct explicit periodic second-order localization corrections to scale-separated AdS$_4$ vacua of massive type IIA supergravity on $T^6/(\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2)$. At first order, the corrections from different O6-plane families simply add. The interactions between intersecting families first enter at second order and could obstruct the continuation of the solution. We find explicit solutions for the warp factor, dilaton, full internal metric and required form fields, including the terms generated by these interactions. The metric at second order contains off-diagonal components. With a common regularization of the singular source terms, we verify the full field equations and the conditions required for a solution on a compact space. Using the pure-spinor formalism, we find that the second-order fields satisfy the supersymmetry conditions accessible at the retained orders.
authors: Aravind Aikot, Timm Wrase

papers.title: $AdS$ Leading Regge Trajectory from String Field Theory
papers.abstract: We determine the $AdS$ mass of the leading Regge trajectory in superstring backgrounds $AdS_5\times S^5$, $AdS_4\times\mathbb{CP}^3$, and $AdS_3\times S^3\times{\cal M}_4$ with pure Ramond-Ramond (RR) flux for both ${\cal M}_4=S^3\times S^1$ and ${\cal M}_4=T^4$, to the second order in the expansion with respect to the background RR flux by solving the linearized equations of motion in closed superstring field theory. The $AdS_5$ and $AdS_4$ results are in a complete agreement with those obtained from the integrability approach to dual gauge theories, thereby providing a nontrivial check of the holographic duality beyond supersymmetry-protected quantities.
authors: Minjae Cho, Jo\~{a}o Gomide, Jaroslav Scheinpflug, Xi Yin

papers.title: Phase matching of high-order harmonics driven by a combined coherent and bright squeezed vacuum field
papers.abstract: High-order harmonic generation (HHG) driven by non-classical light provides new insights into light-matter interactions and paves the way to quantum attosecond spectroscopy. Achieving phase matching is vital for generating bright HHG sources, while it has received comparatively limited attention in quantum-light-driven HHG. In this work, we investigate the phase matching of HHG driven by an intense coherent field combined with a weak bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) field, using a semiclassical ensemble of coherent-field realizations sampled from the Husimi-$Q$ probability distribution. We reveal the physical mechanism behind the distinct pressure dependence of the harmonic yields for odd, even and half-integer sidebands spectral components, as observed in our previous experiment [arXiv:2607.20941]. The simulations and phase-matching model demonstrate that the BSV-induced perturbation of the electron action phase could introduce an additional sub-cycle phase mismatch, such that the amplitude of sub-cycle bursts could be significantly modified by gas pressure after macroscopic propagation, even when the harmonic yield is near the optimum. The resulting amplitude asymmetry of sub-cycle bursts leads to a significant intensity contrast between half-integer sidebands harmonics, manifesting as distinct pressure dependence of their yields. Our findings reveal the phase-matching mechanism in two-color quantum-light-driven HHG, and suggest opportunities for macroscopic control of the non-classical HHG source.
authors: Yaoshun Sun, Shang Ma, Xintong He, Jiaao Cai, Wentao Wang, Mingxuan Li, Xiangyu Tang, Sizuo Luo

papers.title: BPS baryonic tubes in chiral perturbation theory minimally coupled with electrodynamics and a novel crossover
papers.abstract: We derive a novel first-order BPS system (whose solutions are automatically solutions of the second-order field equations) in chiral perturbation theory (CPT) in $(3+1)$ dimensions. These BPS configurations describe baryonic tubes carrying a chiral current along the tubes themselves. Such baryonic tubes can be either homogeneous or modulated along the $z$-axis. We analyze the leading term in CPT, which is the $SU(2)$ non-linear sigma model minimally coupled to electrodynamics. These exact solutions are qualitatively different from the available analytic description of baryonic tubes since, due to their BPS nature, the positions of the energy-density peaks can be arbitrary. In contrast (in the case of the known solutions in the literature), the energy-density peaks' positions are fixed. We compare these two types of baryonic configurations; the relevant parameter that determines which one is energetically favored is the baryonic charge density: for low densities, the old solutions are favorable, while for high densities these novel BPS tubes are energetically favored. The inclusion of the electromagnetic field (together with the corresponding back-reaction on the baryonic tubes) can also be treated analytically. We discuss the differences in the electromagnetic field distribution between the two regions (low and high baryonic density). The analysis of potential terms for the chiral field is detailed in Appendix B.
authors: Fabrizio Canfora, Mart\'in Garrido, Pablo Pais

papers.title: Light-cone distributions of vector and scalar bound states in the Schwinger model from tensor networks
papers.abstract: Light-cone distributions encode the partonic structure of hadrons, but they involve real-time correlations that Euclidean lattice methods cannot access directly. We compute the parton distribution functions (PDFs) and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) of the vector and scalar meson bound states of the massive Schwinger model with tensor networks. Using the Kogut-Susskind lattice Hamiltonian with the gauge field eliminated through Gauss's law, we prepare the vacuum and the mesons as matrix product states and identify the vector and scalar mesons through their charge conjugation and momentum. The gauge-invariant light-cone correlators that define both distributions are evaluated directly in Minkowski space by real-time evolution. The two mesons exhibit qualitatively different light-cone structure, dictated by charge conjugation. The vector meson has a single-peaked PDF and a symmetric LCDA, while the scalar meson has a double-peaked PDF and an antisymmetric LCDA, whose vanishing zeroth moment requires a normalization through its first moment. The decay constants obtained from local matrix elements and from the moments of the LCDAs agree, and approach predictions from nonrelativistic model as the fermion mass increases. For the relatively large masses considered in this work, the PDFs closely follow the squared LCDAs, showing that the mesons are dominated by their valence component. Our results demonstrate tensor networks as a practical route to light-cone distributions of ground-state as well as excited hadrons in low-dimensional gauge theories.
authors: Juan Hormaza, Wenyang Qian

papers.title: Parton Physics in the Schwinger Model from Matrix Product States
papers.abstract: Parton distribution functions (PDFs) and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) encode the non-perturbative structure of hadrons in terms of their partonic constituents. They are defined through matrix elements containing parton operators that are connected by a Wilson line along a light-front direction, which makes them difficult to access in Euclidean lattice calculations. We demonstrate how parton functions can be directly obtained in Minkowski space using the Hamiltonian framework. We compute fermion and antifermion PDFs, LCDAs, and decay constants of the vector meson in the Schwinger model for several fermion masses. States in Hilbert space are efficiently represented by tensor networks, with an expressivity that is systematically controlled by a bond dimension. The light-front Wilson line is implemented as a stepwise evolution on the lattice that alternates spatial shifts of an external charge with Trotterized time-evolution steps acting on a matrix product state. All systematic uncertainties are quantified by varying and extrapolating in the lattice spacing, volume, bond dimension, gauge-field truncation, and Trotter step width. The slow growth of the entanglement entropy makes moderate bond dimensions sufficient, which supports the feasibility of using tensor networks for computing light-front matrix elements in more general settings. We confirm that the computed distributions fulfill the expected normalizations, momentum sum rules, and symmetry properties.
authors: Mari Carmen Ba\~nuls, Krzysztof Cichy, C. -J. David Lin, Manuel Schneider

papers.title: Hadron structure in $1+1$ dimensions from the infinite Hamiltonian lattice
papers.abstract: The internal structure of a hadron is encoded in matrix elements of operators between hadron states of definite momentum. In this paper, we develop a framework for computing such matrix elements in $(1+1)$-dimensional gauge theories by working on an infinite spatial lattice. We apply the method to the massive Schwinger model.
