We benchmark our method against discretized lightcone quantization (DLCQ) at $\theta = 0$, and then use the lattice to study hadrons at $\theta\neq 0$, where DLCQ does not apply. We compute parton distribution functions and gravitational form factors, and both show signatures of hadrons becoming large, loosely-bound states when we set $m$ greater than the critical mass $m_c$ and approach $\theta = \pi$ from below. Moreover, we see the gravitational form factor change from that of a free boson to that of a free Majorana fermion when we set $\theta = \pi$ and approach the 2D Ising critical point at $m=m_c$ from below.
authors: Ross Dempsey

papers.title: A cubic theory of gravity with quasitopological-like properties for compactified cosmologies
papers.abstract: We identify a cubic combination of curvature invariants in dimension $D=7$ that when added to the Einstein-Hilbert action, yields a healthy cosmological evolution in four dimensions after compactification on a constant-curvature internal space of dimension three. For generic backgrounds it leads to fourth-order field equations, nevertheless, on a warped product of a spatially flat, homogeneous and isotropic four-dimensional universe with a constant-curvature space of radius $b(t)$, the constraint is of first order in the scale factor $a(t)$ and in $b(t)$, while the remaining equations are of second order. Requiring this property uniquely singles out the cubic theory. We study the solutions describing a four-dimensional de Sitter Universe in direct product with an internal space of stabilized radius and evaluate its linear stability under time-dependent perturbations, showing that for a given sign of the curvature of the internal space, stability of the static solution fixes the sign of the higher curvature coupling. We also argue that linearized scalar perturbations depending on the spatial coordinates obey equations with at most two time derivatives. Finally, we numerically evolve the homogeneous and isotropic system non-linearly and present evidence that for a positive bare cosmological term $\Lambda_0$ and a hyperbolic compact space, the singularity formation present in GR in this ansatz is pushed into the future by increasing the higher-curvature coupling.
authors: Vicente Aguilar, Fabrizio Canfora, Vicente Garc\'ia, Alex Giacomini, Julio Oliva

papers.title: Beyond the Thermodynamic-Volume Limit in Holographic Complexity
papers.abstract: In the large black hole regime, holographic complexity obeys a thermodynamic-volume scaling law, while the finite-size approach to this limit remains unresolved. In this Letter, we develop an analytic description of finite-size corrections to this scaling for complexity of formation in the complexity=volume (CV) proposal of odd-dimensional equal-spinning Myers-Perry-AdS black holes. We find that the leading finite-size correction retains state dependence that is absent from the limiting thermodynamic-volume law. This correction changes sign at a distinguished Critical Horizon Ratio (CHR), where the generic leading finite-size contribution vanishes and convergence to the thermodynamic-volume law is correspondingly accelerated. We further determine the dimension dependence of the CHR analytically, showing that it approaches a finite nonextremal value at large dimension with a calculable leading finite-dimensional correction. These results show that the finite-size approach can provide a new probe of holographic structure, motivating its exploration across different realizations of holographic complexity and its eventual characterization in the dual field theory.
authors: Di Wu, Robert B. Mann

papers.title: Probing the inner structure of bound states
papers.abstract: We show how constructing a composite particle eigenstate reveals its internal structure. Using quantum subspace expansion (QSE), we optimize states with different sets of operators and use their fidelities with the full QSE state to measure the importance of each added operator type. Taking the scalar meson of the massive Schwinger model as a benchmark, we find that fermion bilinears suffice at large fermion masses. At small masses, two classes of four-fermion operators play important but very different roles: the four fermion operators with two fermions and 2 anti-fermions at small distance give little improvement. In contrast, spatially extended meson-meson operators produce a large gain in state fidelity. Turning to observables, we find that the scalar charge is much more sensitive to the meson-meson operators than e.g. the meson mass. The parton distribution function (PDF) also changes from symmetric to asymmetric about the momentum fraction 1/2, along with the growing importance of meson-meson operators. These results establish QSE as a tool for probing the internal structure of composite particles and connecting it to observable properties.
authors: Yahui Chai, Yibin Guo, Karl Jansen

papers.title: Symmetry-constrained order hierarchy of connected optical responses in a five-level Rydberg-EIT medium
papers.abstract: Determining the connected many-body correlations required for a nonlinear optical response of a given order is a central challenge in interacting open quantum systems. We establish a symmetrybased selection rule for connected optical responses in a driven-dissipative Rydberg-EIT model. Under the specified Lindblad conditions, local phase covariance and zero-probe factorization imply that an n-atom connected contribution to the root optical coherence is forbidden below probe-amplitude order 2n-1. Consequently, optical-response coefficients through fifth order involve at most three-atom connected clusters, without assuming weak interatomic interactions. Direct finite-cluster calculations confirm the predicted lowest allowed orders, while an illustrative Maxwell-propagation calculation shows that triplet contributions can partially oppose pair-induced polarization rotation. Our results establish a rigorous connection between optical perturbation order and the connected many-body sectors that can contribute to it.
authors: Lintian Luo, Weixuan Gu, Yan Li

papers.title: Defining the mathematical family tree with a minimal programming language
papers.abstract: I introduce MLISP, a Turing-complete language with nine single-character commands (a b c d f 0 i j k), and use it to define 88 mathematical structures and a family tree of 65 theories that they model, with three aims: Pedagogy: It presents the mathematical structures in a unified way, with standardized presentation tableaus that define them and axiomatized theories that describe them. Connections: It highlights how they are related in the family tree via added symbols, axioms, etc. While the full tree is obviously infinite, its lower parts naturally separate into six main branches: the relational branch, the algebraic branch, the logic branch, the number branch, the set branch and the continuum branch. Foundations: The definitions, key theorems and models of each entry are verified in Lean. Mathematical structures are defined as equivalence classes of presentations, which in a constructivist spirit are defined in a simple, explicit and self-contained way in standardized presentation tableaus with minimal human baggage. For finite structures, the generating functions are defined by lookup tables. For countably infinite ones, they are instead defined computationally using MLISP, since more complex languages such as Lean are massive overkill for rigorously defining standard arithmetic operations (for example, the program "jibjbfid" defines subtraction). An interactive version is available at https://tegmark.org/mathtree. The Lean code is public, also verifies the correctness of MLISP and includes 43% of the theorems from Mathlib 2026-10-11. \end{abstract}
authors: Max Tegmark (MIT)

papers.title: Exact approach to double- and triple-excitation bound state in open quantum systems
papers.abstract: The determination of multiple-excitation bound state in open quantum systems is of broad interest in quantum physics. While the emergence of double- or triple-excitation bound state has been demonstrated in certain specific situations, their universality and exact solvability remain elusive. In this work, we present an exact approach to the double- or triple-excitation dynamics for interacting quantum emitters coupled to environment by deriving a closed equation. By this exact equation, we identify the critical condition for the emergence of double- or triple-excitation bound state, as well as its relationship to the single-excitation one. Our study not only clearly demonstrates the universality of double- or triple-excitation bound state in open quantum emitter systems, but also reveals the possibility of mediating inter-emitter interactions via multiple-excitation bound states.
authors: X. S. Sun, H. T. Cui, Y. A. Yan, H. Z. Shen

papers.title: Lightest $\Omega$-baryon systems with strangeness $-3$ and $-6$ within the framework of Faddeev and Faddeev--Yakubovsky equations
papers.abstract: We investigate the binding energies and spatial properties of few-body $\Omega$-baryon systems with strangeness $S=-3$ and $S=-6$ using the configuration-space Faddeev and Faddeev--Yakubovsky equations. For the first time, microscopic Faddeev--Yakubovsky calculations are performed for the four- and five-body $\Omega NNN$, $\Omega NNNN$, and $\Omega\Omega NN$ systems. We employ HAL QCD and meson-exchange $\Omega N$ interactions, together with the HAL QCD $\Omega\Omega$ potential, and examine the effects of Coulomb interactions and spin--isospin configurations. The calculations predict substantial enhancement of binding with increasing baryon number, with the most strongly bound $\Omega NNNN$ configurations reaching approximately $60$~MeV and bound $\Omega\Omega NN$ states in the $S=-6$ sector. The results reveal pronounced spin dependence and compact few-body structures, with the $\Omega$ baryon preferentially localized near the center-of-mass. These findings provide new predictions for light multistrange nuclear systems and extend microscopic few-body calculations into the four- and five-body $\Omega$-baryon sectors.
authors: R. Lazauskas, R. Ya. Kezerashvili, I. Filikhin

papers.title: Temporal Soliton Waves in Modern Fiber Laser Systems
papers.abstract: This chapter provides a comprehensive survey of temporal soliton-wave in modern fiber systems. Temporal soliton waves constitute a broad class of nonlinear localized structures in modern fiber laser systems, arising from different balances among dispersion, nonlinearity, gain, loss, spectral filtering, and various forms of cavity coupling. We review the underlying theory, basic experimental findings, and practical methods for the generation, real-time characterization, and active control of soliton families, with a particular focus on recent progress reported for mode-locked fiber-laser platforms. The families covered in the chapter include dissipative solitons, soliton molecules (bound states), and dispersion-managed solitons. For each species, we focus on the pulse energy, duration, stationary and breathing states, and emerging intelligent (machine-learning-assisted) control strategies.
authors: Shilong Liu, Boris Malomed

papers.title: Intrinsic Soft Function in the Continuum and Physical Mass Limit from Lattice QCD
papers.abstract: The intrinsic soft function is a universal nonperturbative ingredient of transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) factorization. Despite substantial progress in lattice QCD studies, a determination with simultaneous control of the continuum, physical-pion-mass, and infinite-momentum limits has remained unavailable. In this work we present the first lattice determination incorporating all these limits within large-momentum effective theory, extracting the intrinsic soft function from a light-meson form factor and quasi-TMD wave functions. A key advance is the use of power-counting-guided axial-vector interpolators, which substantially improve the signal and enable a direct calculation at the physical pion mass. Combined with results from six ensembles spanning four lattice spacings, this improvement allows a precise determination extending to $b_\perp\simeq1.1~\mathrm{fm}$, while remaining consistent with perturbative predictions at short distances. The resulting transverse-distance dependence exhibits an approximately exponential decay, with the decay rate being characterized by an effective scale $\Lambda\simeq0.7~\mathrm{GeV}$ at $\mu=2~\mathrm{GeV}$, providing a quantitative benchmark for nonperturbative Wilson-line dynamics and essential input for precision TMD studies.
authors: Zhi-Chao Gong, Min-Huan Chu, Jun Hua, Xiangdong Ji, Andreas Sch\"afer, Jin-Xin Tan, Han-Zhang Wang, Wei Wang, Jian-Hui Zhang, Mu-Hua Zhang, Qi-An Zhang

papers.title: From outcome exclusion to measurement simulation
papers.abstract: While quantum state exclusion has received considerable attention, the analogous task of measurement outcome exclusion remains less explored. Here we develop a quantitative description of outcome exclusion and extend the resulting framework to obtain necessary and sufficient criteria for measurement simulation by quantum pre-processing and classical post-processing. Our analysis combines two approaches. Algebraic exclusion indices quantify normalized minimum errors in communication tasks with forbidden outputs and yield lower bounds on the number of classical messages required to reproduce the task statistics. Random exclusion profiles provide a statistical description in terms of optimized hypothesis-testing errors and are monotone under both types of processing. This connects outcome exclusion with statistical comparison in the spirit of Blackwell, linking the ability to suppress measurement outcomes to the possibility of simulating one measurement from another.
authors: Kensei Torii, Jiaxi Kuang, Francesco Buscemi

papers.title: SPARK: Spectral Preconditioned Analytic Residual Kolmogorov Arnold Networks for incompressible Navier Stokes equations
papers.abstract: We propose Spectral Jet KAN (SJ-KAN) to reduce the cost of differentiation and the network complexity of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for the Navier-Stokes (NS) equations. The input coordinates are embedded through Chebyshev bases whose spatial derivatives are known in closed form, and all differentiation matrices are computed once for the collocation points before training. A single linear layer compresses the Chebyshev bases into a few latent features, and a single nonlinear Chebyshev Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (CKAN) layer maps these features to the physical variables. Because the basis derivatives are known in advance and the compression is linear, the spatial derivatives in the NS equations are carried through the network analytically by a fixed sequence of matrix products and elementwise operations. Automatic differentiation (AD) is used only in backpropagation, to compute the gradients of the loss with respect to the network weights. We examine three variants of SJ-KAN (JetKAN, JetKAN-F, JetKAN-H), which differ in how the output layer maps the latent features to the physical variables. All variants are tested on the Taylor-Green vortex and on the lid driven cavity at Reynolds numbers Re = 100, 1000, 5000 and 10,000. The results are compared with a KAN that uses AD (PIKAN) and with a standard PINN. The SJ-KAN variants reach comparable or better accuracy than both, with up to 47 times fewer parameters and up to 8.2 times faster training per epoch. SJ-KAN also solves the lid driven cavity flow at Re = 10,000 without any reference data and with fewer than 9,000 trainable parameters. These results show that analytic derivative propagation, a small spectral input layer and a single KAN layer give a faster and simpler solver than methods based on AD, also for flows at high Reynolds numbers.
authors: Dathi Rajasekhar, Thien-Tam Nguyen, Trung Bao Le

papers.title: A colored look at anyons and parastatistics
papers.abstract: Color Lie (super)algebras were introduced in 1978 by Rittenberg and Wyler as generalizations of ordinary Lie (super)algebras. These color structures, graded by abelian groups, are defined by brackets which satisfy generalized Jacobi identities. Only recently the relevance of color Lie (super)algebras to physical applications has been pointed out and proved. The color framework not only describes, but also provides physical signatures for two broad types of parastatistics (particles beyond ordinary bosons/fermions): i) paraparticles which are exchanged via the permutation group and can exist in any space dimension D and ii) anyons (exchanged via the braid group), which exist up to D=2 space dimensions. This paper presents an update of the recent advancements which motivate a brand new "colored look" at questions involving parastatistics and braid statistics.
authors: Francesco Toppan

papers.title: Spatial switching near a four-loop homoclinic bouquet: a mechanism for multi-bump bound states in coupled nonlinear Schr\"odinger systems
papers.abstract: We study how a localized standing wave of a coupled nonlinear Schr\"odinger (CNLS) system can switch between components from one pulse to the next. The standing wave reduction of the CNLS system yields a four-dimensional Hamiltonian system with two reflection symmetries, in which four elementary pulses correspond to a bouquet of homoclinic loops to a saddle. For saddle eigenvalues $\pm\lambda_{1},\pm\lambda_{2}$ satisfying $0<\lambda_{1} < \lambda_{2} < 2\lambda_1$, and under suitable nondegeneracy assumptions, we construct stable and unstable invariant manifolds of the four-loop bouquet. Apart from trajectories asymptotic to the saddle in the corresponding time direction, these manifolds characterize one-sided trapping near the bouquet within the critical Hamiltonian level, namely the level set containing the saddle equilibrium. Both manifolds have codimension one in this level. We prove that if they intersect transversely away from the bouquet, producing super-homoclinic orbits, then there exist infinitely many multi-bump homoclinic orbits to the saddle. These orbits correspond to multi-bump localized standing waves of the CNLS system.
authors: Sajjad Bakrani

papers.title: Geometric Control of Electronic Decoherence in a Chiral Spin-Orbit Coupled Helix
papers.abstract: While chirality is known to impact chemical and optical properties of molecular systems, as well as their biological function, far less is known about its impact on quantum coherence. By considering a chiral helix as a paradigmatic model, we show that within the Born-Markov regime, changing the degree of helical twist can be used to modulate the electronic decoherence rate. Moderate to strong spin-orbit coupling between next-nearest-neighbor sites along the helix are shown to give rise to a strong dependence of the electronic decoherence rate on the degree of chirality. The effect of chirality on electronic decoherence rates is also seen to be strongly impacted by the spatial and temporal correlations between the local environmental fluctuations to which the local excitations along the helix are subject. Our results show that chirality can serve as a tunable design parameter for quantum engineering and highlight the importance role environmental correlations can play in determining how chirality affects electronic decoherence rates.
authors: Neel Moudgal, Nicholas A. Kotov, Eitan Geva

papers.title: On the computation of Green's function in layered elastic media
papers.abstract: We develop a recursive scheme for the computation of Green's function for time-harmonic elastic wave in three-dimensional layered media, based on a matrix basis representation in the Fourier domain and a classic interface reaction-transmission theory. With transversal rotational symmetry preserved, the scheme decouples the Green's function into SH waves and P-SV waves using five scalar functions, which are recursively solved at linear cost with respect to the number of total layers, regardless of the layers the source and target particles locate in. The resulting scheme leads to a stable numerical method ready for Hankel transform evaluation in the spatial domain, constituting a foundation for the analysis and efficient numerical simulation of elastic wave scattering in layered media.
authors: Heng Yuan, Wenzhong Zhang, Bo Wang, Wei Cai

papers.title: A machine learning architecture for scaling of holographic quantum circuits
papers.abstract: We describe an architecture and workflow for learning and generalizing the syntax and parameters of holographic quantum circuits (HQCs), which are natural quantum circuit analogs of classical tensor networks. An HQC uses mid-circuit measurements and resets on a small subset of "physical" qubits whose measurement outcomes become correlated through coupling with a register of persistent "ancilla" qubits, analogous to the physical and bond indices of a tensor network. Hence, an HQC with fixed qubit resources can efficiently generate samples from a large quantum state, and adding qubits to the HQC ansatz has the effect of exponentially increasing the effective bond dimension. Our machine learning approach provides mechanisms for harnessing both features of HQCs by extrapolating the syntax (e.g., a sequence of gates, measurements, and resets) and parameters (e.g., the angles appearing in single-qubit rotations) from a dataset of HQCs to longer or more expressive HQCs. We demonstrate the methodology and its performance on an analytically solvable dataset formed by a vector-valued generalization of the W-state. Finally, we provide an outlook for usage of the methodology for scaling the effective bond dimensions of HQCs in quantum simulation.
authors: Cliff Sun, Michael L. Wall

papers.title: Upper and lower bounds for the critical point of the three-dimensional Ising model
papers.abstract: We prove that the critical point $K_c$ of the nearest-neighbour Ising ferromagnet on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ satisfies $0.2164203058<K_c<0.2293910295$, equivalently $1.541630483<e^{2K_c}<1.582145851$, with both endpoints given by explicit rational numbers. To our knowledge these are the sharpest rigorous bounds available. They improve the classical bounds of Fisher (1967) and of Fr\"ohlich, Simon and Spencer (1976), narrowing the rigorously known interval by a factor of about 3.5, and the interval contains the numerical estimate of the critical point. For the lower bound we refine Fisher's self-avoiding-walk argument. A shortest path in the high-temperature expansion forbids all bonds spanned by its vertices, and the resulting gain is estimated through local correlation integrals and summed over paths by a finite-memory transfer bound. As a by-product, the connective constant of $\mathbb{Z}^3$ is shown to be at most $4.73195$. For the upper bound we prove an infrared bound whose coefficient involves the nearest-neighbour correlation. We keep the zero Fourier mode as an unknown and force it to be positive by exact local relations for the spins on a small shell. The finite inequalities entering the proof are verified in exact rational arithmetic, and the passage to the thermodynamic limit is proved analytically.
authors: Zhongpu Qiu

papers.title: Coherent meson-baryon conversion in a cold-atom non-Abelian lattice gauge simulator
papers.abstract: Quantum chromodynamics (QCD), the non-Abelian gauge theory of quarks and gluons, provides a microscopic description of strongly interacting matter, including hadron structure and dynamics. Real-time dynamics and finite-density properties of these systems remain challenging for conventional Monte Carlo methods because of sign problems. Quantum simulation provides a complementary approach, although circuit depth and noise limit digital implementations and non-Abelian gauge-matter interactions remain difficult to engineer in analog systems. Here we realize a non-Abelian lattice gauge model with dynamical matter in an analog cold-atom simulator and directly observe its hadronic dynamics using site- and spin-resolved quantum gas microscopy. This realization is enabled by harnessing two hyperfine states and site-occupation configurations of 87Rb atoms to jointly encode both matter and gauge fields. We tailor resonant tunneling in a spin-dependent optical superlattice to implement a gauge sector of a truncated one-dimensional SU(2) quantum link model with independently tunable mass and gauge coupling. Leveraging this control, we track the conversion of an initially mesonic state into baryonic or vacuum-like configurations through slow mass ramps. Near resonance, we observe coherent oscillations between mesons and baryon-antibaryon pairs and characterize the conversion efficiency as a function of mass, gauge coupling and net baryon density. Our realization establishes an atomic platform for non-Abelian gauge dynamics, opening a route to microscopic studies of nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly interacting matter.
authors: Tian-Yi Wang, Wei-Yong Zhang, Tie-Jin Zhong, Ming-Gen He, Zhao-Yu Zhou, Hui Sun, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, Jian-Wei Pan

papers.title: Cantor spectrum at a fixed Diophantine frequency
papers.abstract: We establish that the spectrum of one-frequency analytic quasiperiodic Schrodinger operators exhibits Cantor structure in the regime of positive Lyapunov exponents for every fixed Diophantine frequency. The proof follows the general strategy of the gap construction by Goldstein and the second author, but avoids the elimination of double and triple resonances used in the original argument. A novel ingredient is the use of Holder continuity of the integrated density of states (IDS) to exclude energies at which eigenvalue parametrizations in finite volume have small slopes. We also use a linear bound in the volume on the number of zeros of Dirichlet determinants, and a pigeonholing argument to obtain lower bounds on the distances between eigenvalues. The crossing of two translated Rellich functions with opposite slopes produces a local maximum whose eigenfunctions have exponentially small boundary values. Together with finite volume eigenvalue separation, this forces the DOS mass to concentrate near the maximum. However, on an interval of constancy of the acceleration, the Lyapunov exponent is analytic, and hence the DOS is Lipschitz there. This ultimately leads to a contradiction near the maximum.
authors: Rui Han, Wilhelm Schlag, Fan Yang

papers.title: Hybrid correlation generation with finite shared randomness
papers.abstract: Finite shared randomness can reduce the use of a prescribed two-qubit source in a hybrid model. Each party has two fixed binary projective measurements, and the protocol reproduces the resulting joint outcome distributions exactly. The parties choose their classical or quantum interfaces independently, without using the shared label, and keep their classical response functions fixed across branches. Eight labels suffice to preserve all feasible pairs of interface choice probabilities, and this bound is tight. The known classical four-label bound yields minimum-cost saturation. With an unrestricted label budget, the minimum source cost is zero if the target can be reproduced by a purely classical protocol, and one otherwise. For Werner states with identical orthogonal measurement pairs, the exact minimum source cost is obtained for every label budget. The three-label cost jumps at visibility $\frac{2}{3}$. Four labels give zero cost at every visibility. In a family of separable states, the two-label cost varies nonmonotonically with local bias while the full correlation tensor remains fixed. The distributed sampling analysis gives the minimum source cost at each label budget and the minimum worst-case total variation error for classical protocols with at most two shared labels.
authors: Zihan Chen, Shengjun Wu, Zeng-Bing Chen

papers.title: NS5-branes and the black hole/string transition
papers.abstract: Near to the onset of BTZ black hole formation in string theory is a large ensemble of 6d BPS supergravity solutions sourced by slightly separated fundamental strings and Neveu-Schwarz fivebranes. We extend the construction of these geometries to include gauge excitations of the fivebranes, and then study the energetics of D-string solitons in relation to the deconfinement transition of little strings, which are the natural non-abelian degrees of freedom that deconfine in the transition to the black hole phase.
authors: Asad Fayiz, Emil J. Martinec

papers.title: M5-branes wrapped on topological disks from maximal 7D gauged supergravity
papers.abstract: We study new supersymmetric $AdS_5 \times \Sigma$ solutions for $\Sigma$ being a topological disk from the maximal gauged supergravity in seven dimensions with $CSO(p,q,5-p-q)$ gauge groups. These gauged supergravities can be obtained from consistent truncations of eleven-dimensional supergravity on $H^{p,q} \circ T^{5-p-q}$. We find a number of solutions with $SO(2)\times SO(2)$ and $SO(2)\times SO(3)$ symmetries from $SO(5)$ and $SO(3,2)$ gauge groups as well as $SO(2)_{\textrm{diag}}$ symmetric solutions from $SO(5)$ and $SO(4,1)$ gauge groups. Solutions with $SO(2)\times SO(3)$ symmetry preserve $16$ supercharges while the other solutions preserve only $8$ supercharges. Although some of the solutions give a holographic description of the dual $N=1$ SCFTs in four dimensions with finite central charges, most of the solutions describe codimension-2 defects within $N=(2,0)$ theories in six dimensions. For solutions with $SO(2)\times SO(2)$ and $SO(2)_{\textrm{diag}}$ symmetries from $SO(5)$ gauge group for which a complete truncation ansatz of eleven-dimensional supergravity on $S^4$ is known, we also uplift the solutions to eleven dimensions and compute the holographic central charge of the dual four-dimensional $N=1$ SCFT with $SO(2)_{\textrm{diag}}$ symmetry.
authors: Patharadanai Nuchino, Parinya Karndumri

papers.title: Schur saturation and the Clifford ceiling in qudit CSS codes
papers.abstract: Orthogonality-type conditions (triorthogonality in the qubit setting and its prime-dimensional analogues), are the primary algebraic screening criterion for transversal non-Clifford gate constructions in CSS codes. In every known positive construction the certificate is accompanied by a non-Clifford logical gate, leaving open whether a CSS family can satisfy these conditions to arbitrarily high order while admitting no such gate. We answer this question for the class of symmetric spectral CSS codes $Q(A)=CSS(C(A),C(A))$ built from character evaluation on a finite abelian group $G$ with $\exp(G)\mid p-1$, $p\geq 5$ prime. The mechanism is the identity \[C(A)^\perp * C(A)^\perp=\mathbb{F}_p^G,\] which we call Schur saturation of the dual code. It follows from the CSS self-orthogonality condition $A\cap(-A)=\varnothing$ and annihilates every local polynomial phase of degree $\geq 3$. The complete gate-group classification $S^{CSS}_{\leq p-1}(A)=C(A)^\perp \oplus C(Stab(A))$ shows that every strictly CSS-preserving local-diagonal transversal gate lies at level $\leq 2$ of the Clifford hierarchy, a structural bound we call the Clifford ceiling. The criterion extends to arbitrary CSS pairs satisfying $C_Z^\perp * C_Z^\perp=\mathbb{F}_p^n$; the LDPC instance $[[58,16,3]]_5$ is verified computationally. The false-positive character of the orthogonality certificates is sharpest in the Boolean toric family: these codes satisfy $\ell$-orthogonality for $\ell\leq p-2$, yet the non-Clifford sector collapses to zero. The flagship instance $[[64,56,3]]_5$ encodes $56$ logical ququints at rate $R=0.875$ with distance-$3$ protection, passes every orthogonality screening test, and yet admits no local-diagonal non-Clifford gate of any degree. The unique non-Pauli survivor is the uniform quadratic drive $Q_u$, fault-tolerant, logically nontrivial, and Clifford at level $2$, carrying no magic-state resource.
authors: Jos\'e Alberto Guzm\'an-Vega, Juan Carlos Jim\'enez-Cervantes, Eliseo Sarmiento-Rosales

papers.title: Field-Dependent Kinetics, Exact Kinks, and a Moduli-Space Route from Self-Dual Yang-Mills Theory
papers.abstract: We study scalar-field models in 1+1 dimensions with field-dependent kinetic coefficients, motivated by self-dual Yang-Mills (SDYM) theory as a generator of integrable equations. We derive the Euler-Lagrange equation, traveling-wave reduction, and first integral, and solve the inverse problem: given a kinetic structure and a prescribed tanh kink, which potential makes it exact? A quadratic spatial deformation with a canonical temporal sector yields a sextic potential. We obtain: (i) a closed-form kink energy with a Bogomolny-type formulation, independent of the odd parameter, which nonetheless shapes the energy density asymmetrically; (ii) vacuum curvature relations tying the spectrum to the kinetic function at the vacua; (iii) two propositions on speed families, plus a lemma showing single-speed data probe only one combination of the kinetic functions; (iv) a unified admissibility analysis in which positivity of the spatial kinetic function controls hyperbolicity, the potential bound along the kink, and the vacuum masses; (v) a self-adjoint fluctuation operator with a closed-form potential whose asymptotes are the vacuum masses, an exact translation zero mode, and numerical spectra with no negative mode on the admissible region, evidence for spectral stability. Exact SDYM reductions yield integrable equations, whereas the deformed model is generically non-integrable and cannot be an exact reduction. The correct bridge is the moduli-space route: SDYM reduces to the Bogomolny equations, whose BPS monopole and dyon dynamics produce field-dependent kinetic terms; any smooth one-dimensional moduli metric expands, to second order, to the quadratic model studied here, and the Taub-NUT metric of well-separated dyons gives an explicit realization. Full identification of the sextic potential within a specific gauge-theory moduli dynamics remains open and is formulated as a research program.
authors: Ji Wang

papers.title: Mass gap for finite connections in supercritical percolation
papers.abstract: We consider finite open clusters based at the origin in Bernoulli bond percolation on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ for $d\geq3$ at a supercritical value $p>p_c(d)$, whose maximal height in the direction of a unit vector $\pmb{\ell}$ lies in a fixed-width window at distance $u$. Conditioned on this event, we prove that, except with probability exponentially small in $u$, such a cluster is populated at positive density by renewal points. Here, a renewal point $w$ is the only vertex of the cluster in the fixed-width band immediately below the height hyperplane through $w$. The main technical estimate is that, under this conditioning, the absence of a renewal point is exponentially unlikely. From it we derive an exponential mass gap for the irreducible pieces delimited by successive renewal points, and from the mass gap the stated renewal abundance. The mass gap, together with the renewal decomposition and endpoint estimates established here, yields a sharp point-to-point Ornstein--Zernike asymptotic for finite connectivity, with its Gaussian-type power-law correction. The multiplicative prefactor in this asymptotic is positive and real-analytic, and the associated equidecay and Wulff boundaries are real-analytic and strictly convex. The principal innovation of the article is the use of a slide resampling that preserves the conditioned law. The slide acts by cutting the long finite connection at a given $\pmb{\ell}$-height and relocating the upper piece by a random shift. The mass gap is obtained by a delicate analysis of an iterated version of the slide operation along a positive density of attempted heights.
authors: Alexander Fribergh, Alan Hammond

papers.title: QuOptLab: Advancing Quantum Optics Experiments with an AI Agent
papers.abstract: Recent advances in AI-assisted theoretical research suggest that AI agents can contribute to research-level problems. Whether they can also advance experimental research by conducting experiments, analyzing the results, and proposing better experimental designs remains an open question. To address this question, we build a simulated quantum optics laboratory and integrate it with an AI agent in QuOptLab. The laboratory includes optical instruments, a robotic arm, and cameras, enabling the agent to carry out and iteratively refine experiments. We consider two complementary tasks: thin-film thickness measurement in free-space optics and edge-coupler design in integrated photonics. In the thin-film thickness measurement task, the agent repeatedly analyzes measurement results and revises its measurement method, including calibration and data analysis, reducing thickness-estimation error from 7.13 to 0.066~nm$^2$ over six epochs in a classical-interference run. For edge-coupler design, the agent iteratively proposes structural modifications, evaluates the resulting coupling performance, and uses the feedback to guide subsequent revisions, increasing simulated coupling efficiency from 85.81% to 91.98%.
authors: Yuqing Li, Zeguan Wu, Yu Gan, Min Chen, Junyu Liu

papers.title: Beyond Classical Minimax Rates: Quantum Sampling in Gradient-Based Simulation Optimization
papers.abstract: We study gradient-based search for a class of convex simulation optimization problems with gradients estimated from noisy outputs. With independent outputs, the optimal classical convergence rate for the expected objective gap is of order $O(N^{-2/3})$, where $N$ is the query budget. We apply quantum mean estimation to paired finite differences and progressively increase their estimation accuracy as the perturbations shrink, improving the convergence rate to $O(N^{-4/3})$. Furthermore, we show that coupling nearby evaluations improves the classical and quantum convergence rates to $O(N^{-2/(3-\kappa)})$ and $O(N^{-4/(3-\kappa)})$, respectively, where $\kappa\in[0,1]$ describes the variance reduction in paired outputs. Thus, quantum estimation halves the accuracy exponent in query complexity across coupling orders. Moreover, we establish matching lower bounds and show that these accuracy exponents are minimax optimal for fixed decision dimension, even when query locations and batch sizes are adaptive. Reconstruction from feasible differences retains the exponents when every simulation query must be feasible and accommodates boundary optima.
authors: Hao Cao, Jian-Qiang Hu, Mingjie Hu, Qixin Wang

papers.title: Eliminating Incompatibility in Quantum Multiparameter Estimation with Antiparallel Probes
papers.abstract: The simultaneous estimation of multiple parameters is fundamentally constrained by complementarity and measurement incompatibility, which limits the sensitivity of quantum measurement devices by preventing the symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) Cram\'er-Rao bound (CRB) from being saturated. We show that antiparallel probe configurations can overcome this limitation when the dynamics of the parameter encoding preserve the said configurations. We characterise the quantum channels that satisfy this requirement and establish conditions under which such configurations exist and can saturate the SLD-CRB without compromising the quantum Fisher information, leading to a metrological advantage. For qubit probes, we prove that this advantage is present if and only if the encoding channel is unital. We extend this analysis to the two probe, finite dimensional qudit case by considering derivative reversal and transpose map based probe states, as well as more general multiprobe configurations. For each of these cases, we identify conditions under which an advantage exists. Our results establish connections between channel symmetries, probe configurations and the attainability of multiparameter precision limits.
authors: Souradeep Sasmal, Bakmou Lahcen, Kok Chuan Tan

papers.title: Exact Response Theory based on Karhunen-Lo\`eve Expansions for Brownian Oscillators
papers.abstract: We extend Exact Response Theory (ERT) to an overdamped Brownian oscillator driven by thermal white noise. The stochastic forcing is represented by a Karhunen--Lo\`eve series and embedded into an autonomous, augmented phase space using a harmonic auxiliary phase. This representation allows us to construct the ERT dissipation function for fixed mode amplitudes and recover stochastic averages by averaging over the amplitudes and the initial phase. For the variance, we derive the response at finite spectral truncation and show analytically that, with uniform phase sampling, the full-spectrum white-noise limit reproduces the generator-based result for a sudden temperature change. Furthermore, a comparison with first-order linear response theory highlights how this may fail in general. In particular, if the noise-induced variance is quadratic in the noise amplitude, it is completely omitted by linear response. The analysis provides a framework for this model and for studying more general forcing; extensions to non-Markovian dynamics require separate convergence and regularity analyses.
authors: Matteo Colangeli, Lamberto Rondoni, Pasquale Vozza

papers.title: Entanglement structure in conformal Y-junctions
papers.abstract: We study how entanglement constrains energy transmission in conformal Y-junctions using holographic and free-field models. We define pairwise effective central charges from mutual information as a natural extension of the interface entanglement coefficient. For holographic junctions, we formulate a branched RT prescription and show that the resulting entropies satisfy monogamy of mutual information. We find that the pairwise effective central charge does not always bound the corresponding energy transmission, but a correction involving finite tripartite information restores the bound, with a sharp coefficient determined by limiting saturation. Free-boson and Dirac-fermion junctions also violate the pairwise bound, but the tripartite correction fails because the tripartite information is positive or vanishing, respectively. Analytic limits and numerical results instead support a candidate square-root correction based on L-entropy, which vanishes in the holographic complete-leg prescription considered here. We discuss the possibility of a common multipartite information bound in general conformal junctions.
authors: Yan Liu, You-Jie Zeng

papers.title: Universal state merging for almost i.i.d. states
papers.abstract: In quantum state merging, Alice aims to transfer her share of a bipartite state to Bob while preserving the joint state with a purifying reference. For i.i.d. copies of $\rho_{AB}$, the optimal asymptotic net entanglement cost is $S(A|B)_\rho$ ebits per pair. We show that this cost is robust under deviations from exact i.i.d. structure. For every $R>S(A|B)_\rho$, a single sequence of one-way LOCC protocols, depending only on $\rho_{AB}$ and $R$, merges every weakly almost i.i.d. source along $\rho_{AB}$ with vanishing error. The net entanglement cost is at most $nR$ ebits for all sufficiently large blocklengths $n$. This guarantee also covers the Wasserstein and Mazzola--Sutter--Renner subclasses. Each class contains the exact i.i.d. source, so $S(A|B)_\rho$ is optimal for universal merging within each class. More generally, the same protocols achieve vanishing error whenever the two-pair marginal of the permutation-averaged source converges in trace norm to $\rho_{AB}^{\otimes 2}$.
authors: Nilanjana Datta

papers.title: Validity and maximum violation of the entanglement-assisted quantum Singleton bound for linear stabilizer codes
papers.abstract: Entanglement-assisted quantum codes protect quantum information with entangled pairs shared in advance, and the entanglement-assisted quantum Singleton bound of Brun, Devetak and Hsieh is the standard estimate of how many pairs they consume. Codes that violate it at large distance are known. For linear entanglement-assisted stabilizer codes, which include all qubit stabilizer codes of this kind, we determine when the bound holds and how far it can fail. The answer depends on how many qudits, together with the receiver's halves of the pairs, recover the logical qudits. If this number is less than twice the number of logical qudits, the bound holds, also for degenerate codes. If it is exactly twice that, the bound overstates the number of pairs by at most the length of the longest classical maximum distance separable (MDS) code of that dimension, minus the dimension. Codes carrying values and derivatives of polynomials on the projective line attain this maximum whenever the field size is at least that dimension and the MDS conjecture is known for it, which includes every prime and, by a recently announced result, every even field size. If the number is more than twice the number of logical qudits, the violation is bounded in terms of the lengths of classical codes of a given Singleton defect, and the bound is attained for one logical qudit. Apart from cited MDS lengths, the proofs are formalized in the Lean proof assistant.
authors: Jae-Hyun Baek, Byung-Sun Won, Jon-Lark Kim

papers.title: Network topology imposes spectral constraints on collective nonequilibrium responses
papers.abstract: Collective nonequilibrium dynamics in Langevin systems depend on both network topology and stochastic driving. Understanding the role of topology in responses to stochastic driving and in the emergence of nonequilibrium is essential. Starting from the principle of microscopic reversibility and linear Langevin dynamics on networks, we derive a mode decomposition for both the asymmetry of short-time cross-correlations and heat currents at steady state. This decomposition reveals two sources of nonequilibrium---fluctuations of individual modes and correlated fluctuations between distinct modes. For reciprocal networks with independent local driving, we derive two nonequilibrium response operators that yield explicit expressions for the global asymmetry intensity and the entropy production rate. These operators are weighted Laplacians independent of stochastic driving. Their spectra determine attainable upper and lower bounds on nonequilibrium at fixed driving heterogeneity. These bounds are exact for asymmetry intensity at arbitrary deviations from equilibrium and hold to leading order near equilibrium for entropy production rate. Finally, we find that the hierarchical modular organization of human structural connectomes broadens the brain's nonequilibrium operating range, with resting-state brain activity supporting this topological advantage for sustaining a lower nonequilibrium level. Our study provides a basis for understanding biological network organization and designing networks with targeted nonequilibrium operating points.
authors: Dingjie Wu, Yaozu Wang, Rong Wang, Ying Wu

papers.title: Exact transport exponents for random mosaic operators
papers.abstract: We determine the exponentially time-averaged transport exponents of period-two random mosaic operators, with zero potential on the even sites and iid potential on the odd sites. For every bounded, strictly positive, nonconstant single-site law, on one event of probability one, $\beta_f^-(q)=\beta_f^+(q)=\max\{0,2/3-\nu_H(f)/(3q)\}$ for all nonzero finitely supported states $f$ and all $q>0$. The positive odd integer $\nu_H(f)$ is determined by divisibility by $H$ and cancellation against the bounded zero-energy solution. In particular, the large-moment exponent is $2/3$ for every such state, while point sources on the two sublattices have second-moment growth powers $1$ and $1/3$. We obtain matching resolvent bounds by retaining the vanishing orders of two polynomial source channels through the singular normalization at zero energy. We also prove deterministic lower bounds for every bounded positive configuration. No density assumption is imposed on the law.
authors: Fumihiko Nakano, Xu Xia

papers.title: Group classification of a class of systems of nonlinear diffusion equations. I
papers.abstract: We study the Lie symmetries of a class of systems of (1 + 1)-dimensional nonlinear diffusion equations. The equivalence algebra and the kernel of the maximal Lie invariance algebras of this class are found. We prove that there exist exactly nine inequivalent subclasses of this class for which the corresponding diffusion systems admit Lie symmetry extensions. We also carry out the exhaustive group classification of the systems of nonlinear diffusion equations from the first subclass.
authors: Oleksandr A. Voloshyn, Mykola I. Serov, Olena O. Vaneeva

papers.title: Resolvent reconstruction of minimal strings beyond KdV II: D series models
papers.abstract: Three-state Potts gravity and tetracritical Ising gravity have the same central charge and the same conformal spectral curve. What distinguishes their amplitudes once a handle or a boundary is added? We answer this question by extending Johnson's differential-equation approach, in the reconstruction form developed in Part I for the reduced KP hierarchies, to D-series minimal strings. Their spatial operator is a pseudo-differential pencil with a nonlocal Pfaffian term, and the classical energy acquires a second pole at zero momentum. Regularity at both poles fixes the quantum corrections uniquely, ordinary string equations supply them, and the ordinary D flows add boundaries in a way that matches the tau function. At genus one the closed free energy follows from the pencil as a sum of logarithms of critical-value velocities. The two theories differ through the origin of the curve, which the D theory counts as two canonical directions, and through the pairing of every point with its reflection. We follow the origin contribution through the free energies to genus three, the one-holed torus and the torus one-point amplitudes, and in the primary range the latter reproduce the formulas conjectured from worldsheet numerics for both series.
authors: Wasif Ahmed, Joydeep Naskar

papers.title: Toward light-controlled transverse Wigner ordering in attosecond electron beams
papers.abstract: Kinetic fluctuations and space-charge expansion hinder Wigner ordering in free-electron beams. Here we propose a laser-driven route toward transient, substrate-free Wigner ordering that combines photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM) attosecond bunching, synchronized magnetic focusing, and spatial preconditioning. Classical relaxation and zero-temperature fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo trap benchmarks show that sixfold order survives quantum fluctuations from 1 T to sub-Tesla fields, defining ultrafast preparation targets.
authors: Yiming Pan, Jiapeng Yang, Hao Geng

papers.title: Low-Degree Torus Approximations of the AND Function and $\mathsf{ACC}^0$ Circuits
papers.abstract: Torus polynomials, real polynomials evaluated modulo one, were proposed by Bhrushundi, Hosseini, Lovett, and Rao as a route to $\mathsf{ACC}^0$ lower bounds. We prove degree upper bounds for torus polynomials approximating a function on every input. First, for every $\epsilon\in(0,1/4)$, $\mathsf{AND}_n/2$ has an $\epsilon$-approximating torus polynomial of degree $O(\log(n/\epsilon))$, improving the previous $O(\log^2(n/\epsilon))$. This is optimal up to constant factors for inverse-polynomial error, by a lower bound of Krishan and Vishwanathan, and refutes two superlogarithmic-degree conjectures of Krishan and Sarma. Second, for every Boolean function $g$ computed by a depth-$d$, size-$s$ $\mathsf{AC}^0[m]$ circuit, $g/2$ has an $\epsilon$-approximating torus polynomial of degree at most $C_m^d(\log s)^{\max\{1,\mu-1\}d}\log(1/\epsilon)$, where $\mu$ is the number of distinct prime factors of $m$ and $C_m$ depends only on $m$. This improves the bound $(\log s)^{O_m(d^2)}(\log(1/\epsilon))^{O_m(d)}$ of Bhrushundi, Hosseini, Lovett, and Rao, making the exponent of $\log s$ linear in the depth and the dependence on $\log(1/\epsilon)$ linear. Both proofs sample terms of a Fourier expansion and approximate them by low-degree torus polynomials. A torus approximation of degree $D$ can be written as a linear combination of at most $(n+1)^D$ parities, called a periodic Fourier representation, which is known to give a non-adaptive measurement-based quantum computation with linear side-processing using one qubit per parity. Hence every $\mathsf{ACC}^0$ function can be computed with quasipolynomially many qubits and inverse-polynomial error probability on every input. Conversely, we prove that a periodic Fourier representation with $r$ parities and error probability $\epsilon$ gives a torus approximation of degree $O(\log(r/\epsilon))$, so the two notions are equivalent.
authors: Shuhei Osaki, Ryuhei Mori

papers.title: Transfer tensor description of driven inhomogeneous quantum systems
papers.abstract: The transfer tensor method (TTM) extrapolates open quantum system dynamics from short-time trajectories by encoding memory effects in a discrete hierarchy of transfer tensors. Standard TTM relies on time-translational invariance (TTI) of the dynamical maps, which is broken by time-dependent driving or coherent control. We generalize TTM to time-inhomogeneous and periodically driven systems with a two-time transfer tensor hierarchy $\mathcal{T}(n,k)$. For driving with period $t_0$, sub-stroboscopic sampling ($\Delta t = t_0/N_c$) restores a block TTI, $\mathcal{T}(n+mN_c, k+mN_c) = \mathcal{T}(n,k)$, so that only $N_c$ starting-time branches must be learned. Averaging over the driving phase (or start time), termed temporal homogenization, restores single-index TTI at the price of phase-induced memory that combines non-additively with that of static disorder. We study two systems. (i) In an inhomogeneously broadened two-level ensemble driven beyond the rotating-wave approximation (RWA), the phase-induced memory scales with the square of the Rabi coupling and the disorder-induced memory with the square of the inhomogeneous width. The phase-induced memory is frame dependent: in the drive's rotating frame it arises solely from counter-rotating terms and vanishes under the RWA, whereas in the lab frame it largely survives the RWA. (ii) In a driven tight-binding chain at the Dunlap--Kenkre condition, the clean chain is stroboscopically frozen, whereas sub-stroboscopic tensors show that dynamical localization is enforced by delayed, period-commensurate refocusing in the memory kernel, in contrast to the immediate backflow of Anderson localization. A generalized outgoing pseudoflux tracks the non-monotonic dependence of the spreading on disorder: moderate disorder breaks the refocusing and lets the particle spread over a larger but finite region, whereas strong disorder confines it.
authors: Ferdos Fessahaye, Rajesh Dutta, Michelle Anderson, Chern Chuang

papers.title: Entanglement between distant spins in a polarized magnet forms a $d$-wave clover
papers.abstract: Spin-orbit coupling makes a polarized magnet a source of virtual spin-flip pairs. These pairs entangle distant spins: the symmetry of the coupling fixes the angular pattern, and the flips they leave behind end it at a distance of order the inverse spin-orbit angle. For a spin-1/2 square-lattice ferromagnet we prove, at leading order, a d-wave inverse-square law, 1.376 times the spin-wave amplitude, a clover-shaped entangled region, exact without the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya term, and that each spin's entanglement is entirely pairwise. Four qubits can test the d-wave signs at present error rates.
authors: Alan Zhang, Ye Zhou

papers.title: The polarization bundle of a bending ray: nested projections and helicity Chern numbers
papers.abstract: We consider a ray propagating in a weakly anisotropic, possibly absorbing medium. The transverse planes of the propagation directions form a rank-two complex vector bundle $E_\perp$ over the sphere $S^2$ of directions. The polarization states are the points of $Z=\mathbb{CP}(E_\perp)$. Projecting the flat derivative of $\mathbb{C}^3$ onto $E_\perp$ gives a connection $D$, the complexified Levi-Civita connection of $S^2$, whose holonomy is the Rytov rotation. Projecting $D$ onto a polarization line gives the connection of the tautological line bundle over $Z$, whose holonomy is the Pancharatnam--Berry phase. For the horizontal distribution defined by $D$, the curvature of this bundle is $i\omega_{\mathrm{FS}}$ on the vertical part, $i s_3\,\omega$ on the horizontal part, and zero on the mixed part. Here $\omega_{\mathrm{FS}}$ is the Fubini--Study form, $\omega$ the area form of $S^2$, and $s_3$ the circular Stokes parameter. The Rytov rotation, the Pancharatnam--Berry phase and the Chern numbers $c_1(L_\pm)=\mp 2$ are all obtained from this curvature. Restricted to the helicity sections, it gives the obstruction to a globally smooth circular Jones vector, although the circular polarization states are globally defined.
authors: Didier Felbacq, Emmanuel Rousseau

papers.title: Magnetometry and slow light in PT-symmetric cavity optomechanics
papers.abstract: The generation of optical higher-order sidebands, which produces new frequencies with regular spectral separation, holds significant promise for applications in optical communication and quantum metrology. We investigate second-order sideband generation and tunable slow-fast light effects in a parity-time (PT)-symmetric cavity optomechanics and propose an enhanced magnetometer scheme. We demonstrate that the PT-symmetric structure, an external magnetic field, and the photon tunneling strength provide powerful and flexible control over both the second-order sideband efficiency, as well as the broadening and switching of slow-fast light propagation. Operating in the PT-symmetry-protected phases, our magnetometer based on the second-order sideband achieves a theoretical sensitivity at the picotesla level, surpassing the performance of previous optomechanical approaches. Our results offer new strategies for magnetic field sensing and optical transmission control, paving the way toward applications in quantum sensing and optical information storage.
authors: Yuguo Su, Tianshun Tan, Yiying Yan, Hengyan Wang, Elijah Omollo Ayieta, Szabolcs Kelemen, Slobodan Radosevic, JunYan Luo, Yi-Xiao Huang, Xingyu Zhang

papers.title: Compressional-shear wave interference and wave suppression at exceptional-point gaps
papers.abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) in complex elastic materials signify the coalescence of compressional and shear modes and bound a frequency gap where waves become evanescent. While their effects on wave propagation have been extensively studied, the physical mechanisms underlying their existence remain elusive. In this Letter, employing a transfer matrix formulation combined with Bloch's theorem, we demonstrate that the gaps bounded by EPs in layered media originate from destructive interference between the compressional and shear wave fields. We further reveal that the corresponding wavenumbers satisfy a Bragg-like condition with the unit cell thickness, causing the total wave field to become stationary, forming a standing wave. Finally, a finite layered medium is considered, where this mechanism is shown to manifest as forbidden wave propagation for both modes in the gap. These results provide a direct physical interpretation of EPs.
authors: Gabriel N\'u\~nez, William J. Parnell, Rapha\"el C. Assier

papers.title: Holographic Entanglement Entropy of Network CFT
papers.abstract: Miao et al. \cite{Guo:2025sbm, Guo:2026prm} proposed the AdS/NCFT correspondence, which explores the gravity dual of conformal field theories defined on networks. While previous studies investigated this model within Einstein and Gauss-Bonnet gravity (first- and second-order Lovelock gravity), in this paper, we generalize the framework to higher-order Lovelock gravity and more complex network structures. We derive the extremal and junction conditions for generalized Ryu-Takayanagi (RT) surfaces in third-order Lovelock gravity, which can be naturally extended to arbitrary higher-order Lovelock theories. Focusing on a network model comprising one node and three branches, we numerically investigate the relationship between the network holographic entanglement entropy (HEE) and gravitational coupling coefficients. Furthermore, by analyzing the HEE across various network configurations, we find that the primary structural feature affecting the network HEE is the presence of internal nodes within line-shaped networks. Our results indicate that the network HEE decreases as the number or depth of internal branches increases.
authors: Zhi-Rong Deng, Jie Yang

papers.title: Augmented Imaginary-Time Evolution of Neural Quantum States with Implicit Time Steps
papers.abstract: Finding the ground states of quantum many-body systems remains a central challenge in physics and quantum chemistry. Imaginary-time evolution (ITE) offers a natural, widely used route, but its convergence is typically asymptotic. Variational approaches restrict this evolution to parameterized manifolds, with neural quantum states (NQS) providing flexible representations commonly optimized via stochastic reconfiguration (SR). Their performance depends on the geometry of the variational manifold, the convergence properties of ITE, and the stability of finite-step explicit (forward) integrators. By exploiting local geometric information of the energy landscape, the recently introduced augmented imaginary-time evolution (AITE) can, in principle, reach the ground state in finite imaginary time. To exploit the accelerated convergence of AITE in NQS optimization, we first combine an implicit Euler step with Galerkin projection to derive an implicit SR scheme that permits large, stable steps and substantially outperforms conventional methods. We use it to formulate an implicit version of AITE and show that its acceleration persists under variational projection and finite-step integration with asymptotically quadratic convergence of the energy error. With finite sampling, implicit schemes yield consistent gains, and implicit AITE becomes increasingly advantageous.
authors: Maksymilian Kliczkowski, Thomas D. K\"uhne, Fedor \v{S}imkovic IV, Prachi Sharma, Carlos L. Benavides-Riveros, Werner Dobrautz

papers.title: The role of composition rules in an axiomatic derivation of quantum mechanics
papers.abstract: Local discriminability and purification are two key axioms in an information-theoretic axiomatization of quantum mechanics as proposed by G. M. D'Ariano et al. (Quantum Theory from First Principles, 2017). Both of them refer to compound systems, the theory of which is rather directly assumed to be given by the tensor product structure. This structure, though well understood, should, however, be based on a more careful study of formal composition rules describing how local effects can be embedded into the compound effect space and how to reduce joint states onto subsystems. In that we follow the earlier work of T. Matolcsi, (Acta Sci. Math., 1975), and D. Aerts and I. Daubechies, (Helvetica Physica Acta, 1978), as summarized, e.g., in The Logic of Quantum Mechanics, 1981, by E. Beltrametti and G. Cassinelli. We also establish axioms of local discrimination stating that compound states can be told apart by local measurements the notion of which we also formally define. The purification axioms first introduced as axioms of quantum mechanics by D'Ariano et al. are also rewritten in a weaker form which we believe could be fruitful for future axiomatizations. These reformulations bring us closer to proper tensor product structures for joint state and effect spaces, so that the embedding map for states factors through the projective tensor product of the local state spaces and the embedding map for effects factors through the injective tensor product of the local effect spaces. We also discuss the case of multipartite composition axioms and associativity properties required in these settings.
authors: Erkka Haapasalo, Pekka Lahti, Juha-Pekka Pellonp\"a\"a

papers.title: Improving Quantum Oblivious Transfer using Zero-Knowledge Proofs
papers.abstract: While quantum protocols for oblivious transfer can be built from weaker assumptions than classical ones, the current protocols remain highly impractical due to stringent security bounds that demand a large amount of quantum communication. In this work, we propose an enhancement to quantum oblivious transfer protocols by leveraging zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs). At a high level, we modify the protocol such that the receiver proves that they are following honestly some crucial steps of the protocols, without revealing extra information to the sender. This yields a tighter security bound against a malicious receiver. For practical scenarios with a fixed security target, this approach reduces the amount of required quantum communication by one to two orders of magnitude, depending on the specific parameters. Furthermore, the benefits of our approach become particularly pronounced at higher qubit error rates, and our proposal even extends the maximum tolerable error rate of the quantum channel from approximately 3.5% to about 9%. The ZKP, however, introduces a substantial computational overhead, estimated to significantly exceed the acquisition time of the protocol, which is usually the primary bottleneck. To address this limitation, we also introduce a variant that serves as a tunable trade-off between the protocol with and without our modification. This enables precise adjustment of the computational overhead while still retaining significant, albeit moderately reduced, efficiency gains.
authors: Alex Bredariol Grilo, Lucas Hanouz, Anne Marin

papers.title: Rydberg Constraint Ensembles for Nonnative Binary Optimization
papers.abstract: Rydberg blockade can exclude the configuration that minimizes a binary objective. We expand its finite penalties into a weighted ensemble of exclusion graphs. The full ensemble preserves the ground energy, and the interactions remaining on each graph set its local detunings. In simulations of two coupled squares, reversing a target coupling leaves the single-site energy slopes at uniform occupation unchanged, yet a collective mode of the residual interactions switches the favored diagonals from aligned to opposed. On 32 held-out twelve-site targets, the simulated probability of recovering a ground state in 128 shots averages 69.82\% with residual detunings and 24.31\% with a tuned uniform pulse. By scoring the pooled samples under the original objective, we can use these native layouts to search for ground states of a Hamiltonian that none implements alone.
authors: Zecheng Shen

papers.title: A quantum-inspired spiking variational autoencoder for robust anomaly detection at the LHC
papers.abstract: Model-agnostic searches for new physics at the Large Hadron Collider utilise unsupervised anomaly detection, where quantum and neuromorphic detectors represent potential approaches. We develop the first fully spiking variational autoencoder, a quantum-inspired spiking variational autoencoder (QSVAE), built on the quantum-inspired leaky integrate-and-fire (QLIF) neuron. In this work we recast the neuron from a measurement-based circuit to a differentiable computational unit. This neuron is benchmarked against other classical, spiking, and quantum models on an LHC di-jet latent space. We show that under noise perturbations the QLIF network retains $0.95$ of its clean accuracy, while accuracy retention for twelve classical models falls to $0.74$-$0.85$. The QLIF anomaly scores respond $3.5$-fold less to the noise perturbation than any of the control model's scores. We compare against a periodic classical control that reproduces the QLIF effect, isolating it to the $\sin^2$ membrane map. This membrane map is a native regulariser that decouples robustness from model capacity supplied by the qubit state space. We demonstrate this through several benchmarks and ablation studies to characterise the performance landscape of the quantum-neuromorphic model space.
authors: Dean Brand, Donovan Slabbert, Chanelle Matadah Manfouo, Francesco Petruccione

papers.title: Relaxation dynamics of the impurity momentum in a one-dimensional Fermi gas
papers.abstract: We consider a single mobile impurity coupled by a repulsive contact interaction to a gas of free spinless fermions of equal mass in one dimension. Using the determinant overlaps between the interacting eigenstates and free-fermion states, we derive closed determinant formulas for the matrix elements of the impurity momentum operator and of its square between arbitrary Bethe-ansatz eigenstates of a finite system. At infinite coupling we prove a selection rule: both operators have vanishing matrix elements between distinct eigenstates that share the same rapidity, and every eigenstate carries the per-particle share of the total momentum. For an impurity injected into the Fermi sea we have the following: at infinite coupling the average impurity momentum relaxes completely in the thermodynamic limit, while at finite coupling relaxation remains incomplete. The closed-form matrix elements turn the spectral representation of the average impurity momentum into explicit finite sums over eigenstates. We evaluate the post-injection dynamics, resolve the quantum-flutter oscillations and the approach towards the diagonal-ensemble value, and map the stationary momentum as a function of the injection momentum and the coupling. Finally, we analyse the thermodynamic limit and its asymptotics as an integral over Fredholm determinants.
authors: Felipe Taha Sant'Ana

papers.title: Dynamic scaling behaviors induced by periodic drivings at continuous Ising quantum transitions
papers.abstract: We investigate the out-of-equilibrium scaling behaviors induced by periodic driving protocols in quantum many-body systems near continuous quantum phase transitions at zero temperature. We consider two paradigmatic one-dimensional systems: the quantum Ising chain subject to periodic longitudinal fields and the Kitaev fermionic wire with periodically driven chemical potentials, equivalent to a quantum Ising chain with a periodic transverse field. Within a renormalization-group (RG) framework, we develop a dynamic scaling theory for both finite-size systems and the thermodynamic limit, identifying scaling variables associated with the driving amplitude and period. We distinguish between protocols that break the global ${\mathbb Z}_2$ symmetry by coupling to the order parameter and those that preserve it. These two classes of driving exhibit distinct scaling behaviors, with power-law exponents determined by the RG dimensions of the corresponding perturbations. We verify the proposed dynamic scaling theory through numerical simulations of both smooth single-frequency and discontinuous square-wave periodic drivings.
authors: Andrea Pelissetto, Davide Rossini, Ettore Vicari

papers.title: Semi-Implicit Finite Volume Central Scheme for Hyperbolic Systems of Balance Laws with Adjustable Free Parameter approximation to relaxed source term
papers.abstract: This study develops a generalized framework for constructing a three-stage predictor-corrector finite volume scheme for solving hyperbolic balance laws with stiff relaxation source terms. The proposed scheme extends the central Nessyahu-Tadmor (NT) framework for the nonhomogeneous part of PDE and the integrals of the source terms are computed using an undetermined coefficient approach to introduce a free parameter \(\alpha\), which offers flexibility in formulation. A unified theoretical analysis is then carried out to characterize the properties of the resulting scheme and determine the admissible range of \(\alpha\). Specifically, uniform consistency and asymptotic properties are investigated along with $A$ -stability and $L$-stability, with the corresponding theoretical constraints combined to establish a common admissible range for the free parameter. The numerical performance of the scheme is subsequently evaluated through a sequence of test problems. Smooth-solution tests are used to assess its accuracy, while one-dimensional benchmark problems arising from different mathematical models are considered to examine its performance in comparison with existing numerical schemes. The assessment is further extended to ten two-dimensional Riemann problems to investigate the ability of the scheme to capture shocks and complex wave interactions along with computational cost.
authors: Sudipta Sahu, Rathan Samala

papers.title: Quantum Tautochrone for photons and atoms
papers.abstract: The tautochrone problem, in which the travel time to a common point is independent of the starting position, has served as a foundational model in classical mechanics. Here we establish its quantum counterpart in engineered photonic waveguide arrays and atomic optical lattices, where nonuniform couplings drive photons and particles launched from different positions to converge simultaneously at a common site. Using higher-order correlation functions, we show that this quantum tautochrone effect holds for both bosons and fermions, with quantum statistics governing the character of the convergence: bosons converge onto the same site, while fermions, constrained by Pauli exclusion, gather at neighboring sites. For bosonic atoms, we further show how the tautochrone dynamics is shaped by lattice inhomogeneity, phase-space structure, and on-site interactions.
authors: Georgios K. Simopoulos, Georgios E. Pavlou, Ioannis Kiorpelidis, Georgios A. Siviloglou, Konstantinos G. Makris

papers.title: D0-brane bound states in Matrix theory: nonperturbative bounds on matrix extent, noncommutativity and spatial shape
papers.abstract: In Matrix theory, a single eleven-dimensional supergraviton is associated with a BPS bound state of D0-branes. Assuming the existence of a normalized physical BPS state, we derive nonperturbative bounds on its matrix extent, noncommutativity and spatial shape from supersymmetry in the BFSS model. The probability of matrix configurations smaller than a fixed fraction of an explicit extent scale is exponentially suppressed in the square of the number $N$ of D0-branes. In Yang-Mills variables, this scale for the trace-normalized extent is of order the cube root of the 't Hooft coupling. Relative noncommutativity, measured by a dimensionless commutator ratio, has an expectation bounded by a quantity of order the inverse of $N$, and its probability of exceeding a sufficiently large fixed multiple of the inverse of $N$ vanishes at large $N$. Concentration of the matrix extent along a fixed number of principal directions fewer than nine at large $N$ requires the total extent relative to a corresponding reference scale to diverge in probability. It also requires relative noncommutativity to be suppressed more strongly than the inverse of $N$, in every fixed finite moment of order at least one. These bounds apply to the full quantum wave function, including off-diagonal matrix degrees of freedom, and constrain the quantum structure of D0-brane bound states and the possible large-$N$ matrix geometries in Matrix theory.
authors: Tetsuyuki Muramatsu

papers.title: Quantum Coherence and Basis-Dependent Correlations in Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: Quantum coherence and quantum correlations are two fundamental features of quantum systems and are closely related in various quantum information tasks. In general, due to the existence of correlations, the amount of coherence in a bipartite state should be no less than that in the reduced states. We focus on what types of states have an equal amount of coherence in the global state and the local states. For such states, the basis-dependent correlations (the difference between the coherence of a bipartite state and its reduced state with respect to a set of standard orthogonal local bases) vanish. Based on the Tsallis relative entropy coherence measure, we prove that block-diagonal product states exhibit vanishing basis-dependent correlations. Furthermore, we establish an equivalence between the absence of basis-dependent correlations and the block-diagonal product structure in a special case. We then consider the coherence measure based on quantum Fisher information and show that block?diagonal product states again lead to vanishing basis-dependent correlations, while in the two-qubit case the vanishing condition constrains the state to a broader block-diagonal-like product structure. These results provide a structural characterization of bipartite states with vanishing basis-dependent correlations under different coherence measures.
authors: Zi-Han Chen, Hui Zhao, Shao-Ming Fei, Zhi-Xi Wang, Mei-Ming Zhang

papers.title: AI-assisted formal proofs for static and time-dependent density functional theory on lattices
papers.abstract: The Hohenberg-Kohn theorem fails on lattices, where two potentials that differ by more than a constant can share a ground state. We prove that such potentials are exceptional. We consider spinless fermions on any connected lattice, at any filling other than empty or full, with hopping amplitudes of a common sign and any density-density interaction. The potentials whose ground state is shared with a potential differing by more than a constant lie in a closed, nowhere dense set of zero Lebesgue measure. The densities of non-degenerate shared ground states form a set of codimension at least two. The statement about the potentials also holds for the Kohn-Sham potential and for spin-density functional theory, where a uniform shift of the magnetic field is the only additional freedom. In time-dependent density functional theory on lattices, we show that not every ground state of a connected lattice can serve as the initial state of the density-potential map. A counterexample is the ground state of two fermions on a square that Penz and van Leeuwen found as a counterexample to the Hohenberg-Kohn theorem. For almost every static potential, however, every real ground state can serve as an initial state, also for spin-resolved densities. We also give formal proofs that the time-dependent Kohn-Sham potential exists, locally in time, for almost every static Kohn-Sham potential, and of known results: local existence and uniqueness of the time-dependent potential for an admissible initial state, continuation in time up to the boundary of the set of admissible states, and the convergence properties of a regularized Kohn-Sham iteration. All theorems and propositions are formalized in the proof assistant Lean 4 and checked by computer.
authors: Miguel A. L. Marques, Irene D'Amico, Stefano Pittalis

papers.title: The DBI critical electric field in stationary non-diagonal geometries
papers.abstract: We investigate the critical electric field for the holographic Schwinger effect in general stationary non-diagonal geometries. We show that, in such backgrounds, the DBI reality condition must be formulated in terms of the electric field measured in a local orthonormal frame, since the coordinate components of the field strength need not represent a purely electric field in that frame. The critical field measured in the orthonormal frame takes the universal value \(E_{\mathrm{proper},c}=T_F\), while its coordinate expression depends on the background geometry. The resulting critical field is independently confirmed by the holographic potential analysis, through the disappearance of the potential barrier. We further illustrate the general prescription using the planar limit and the global rotating Myers--Perry--AdS geometry, which exhibit different types of metric mixing.
