authors: Nabaraj Khatri, Dilip Ojha, Rajib Tripathi, Kismat K. C, Ashish Khanal

papers.title: Fisher information in the flux landscape
papers.abstract: We quantify the fine-tuning of the flux superpotential in Type IIB Calabi-Yau orientifold compactifications using the Fisher Information Metric. Treating the background fluxes as model parameters and the magnitude of the superpotential as the physical observable, we show that the Fisher matrix admits a unique non-zero eigenvalue that bounds the superpotential from above and factorises into axio-dilaton, complex structure components and a bounded factor depending on both moduli and the phase of the superpotential. In the canonical duality frame and over the full flux lattice, this eigenvalue grows linearly with the inverse string coupling and cubically with the complex structure saxions. Specialising to a two modulus orientifold of the degree 18 hypersurface in $\mathbb{P}^4(1,1,1,6,9)$ at large complex structure, we combine the flux integrality with the D3-brane tadpole condition to show that several flux components, including the one driving this growth, are forced to vanish across deep moduli space patches, truncating the twelve-dimensional flux lattice to an eight-dimensional sublattice. The Fisher eigenvalue restricted to these admissible flux directions either approaches a constant or grows at most linearly, much more slowly than over the full lattice.
authors: Martin Carrascal, Radu Tatar

papers.title: Dirac Propagation for Simulating Fermionic Observables under Particle-Number-Conserving Unitaries
papers.abstract: Simulating the dynamics of interacting fermions remains a central computational challenge across physics and chemistry. We introduce Dirac propagation, a classical method that simulates local observables in fermionic systems subject to particle-number-conserving unitaries. We show that, in the operator expansion, strings with weights above the total particle number can be discarded without incurring any error in the final expectation value. This exact cutoff bounds the number of retained strings polynomially in the number of modes at fixed particle number, including for interacting dynamics. The formalism combines a compact representation with explicit expressions for interacting gates and exact treatment of number-conserving fermionic Gaussian and Clifford unitaries. This framework offers an approach to simulating fermionic many-body dynamics and classically benchmarking fermionic quantum circuits.
authors: G Arnav Naidu, Matteo D'Anna, Adri\'an P\'erez-Salinas, Jannes Nys, Juan Carrasquilla

papers.title: From Fermions to Vortices: Microscopic Simulations of Phase Ordering in a d-Wave Superconductor
papers.abstract: Describing bath-induced superconducting phase ordering directly from a microscopic fermionic Hamiltonian remains a formidable challenge. Here we develop a microscopic framework for this problem using the recently introduced adiabatic variational principle (AVP) and demonstrate its application to a two-dimensional $d$-wave superconductor. The central construction maps evolving, spatially inhomogeneous bond-pairing fields onto constrained Bogoliubov-de Gennes states, with the associated Lagrange multipliers determining the thermodynamic driving forces. This enables dissipative evolution of the superconducting order while retaining its microscopic electronic structure, without assuming a phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau free-energy functional. Starting from disordered pairing configurations, we resolve the emergence of phase coherence through vortex-antivortex annihilation and the accompanying evolution of local electronic spectra. Vortex decay and dynamical scaling recover the characteristic kinetics of two-dimensional phase ordering, providing a nontrivial benchmark of the framework. The solver-independent AVP formulation opens a route to microscopic studies of dissipative ordering and metastability in superconductors with intertwined stripe and pair-density-wave orders.
authors: Ali Rayat, Gia-Wei Chern

papers.title: Theory-Informed Quantum Error Mitigation for Shor Order Finding with Fourier Neural Operators
papers.abstract: Quantum noise distorts the distribution of circuit measurement outcomes, often leaving enough information to infer the algorithm's correct result. To recover this latent information from the noisy distribution in Shor order finding, we introduce a theory-informed quantum error mitigation method. We model how circuit errors shift, broaden, or weaken peaks in the output distribution. These models guide both the generation of synthetic training data and the design of a Fourier neural operator with a learned gain that attenuates or amplifies higher retained Fourier modes. We score each candidate order by averaging the correlations between its ideal distribution and the distributions measured in three circuit executions. The network adjusts these scores to guide the order estimate and determine the weights of a normalized mixture of the ideal distributions. On 1,351 simulated test cases for general modular exponentiation, held out by circuit configuration, exact order recovery rises from 19% to 34%, and the median Jensen-Shannon divergence from the ideal distribution falls by 50%, from 0.64 to 0.32. On 101 Mersenne rotation circuits executed across five IBM quantum processors, a separate model trained and calibrated in simulation increases the number of correct order estimates from 35 to 53. Algorithmic structure can remain recoverable even when noise makes it barely visible.
authors: Stefano Markidis, Qingxin Yang, Erik {\AA}sgrim, Ivy Peng

papers.title: Entanglement Asymmetry and the Quantum Mpemba Effect in Inhomogeneous Quenches
papers.abstract: Entanglement asymmetry is a powerful probe of symmetry breaking and its dynamical restoration following quantum quenches. While extensively studied for homogeneous initial states, its evolution from inhomogeneous initial configurations remains largely unexplored. We investigate a spin-$1/2$ XX chain whose two halves are initially prepared in tilted ferromagnetic states with different tilt angles. Combining generalized hydrodynamics (GHD) and the quasiparticle picture with exact fermionic correlation-matrix calculations, we study the dynamics of entanglement asymmetry. We find good agreement between the two approaches for generic initial configurations and observe the quantum Mpemba effect, whereby states with stronger initial symmetry breaking can restore the symmetry faster. This effect now depends on the subsystem position: while the homogeneous behavior is recovered when the subsystem lies entirely within one of the initially tilted halves, the entanglement-asymmetry curves for subsystems straddling the interface can exhibit multiple crossings or no crossings at all. A notable exception occurs for subsystems entirely within an initially non-tilted half. In this case, GHD predicts vanishing asymmetry, but the exact dynamics generates a small, nonzero asymmetry that can develop a plateau before decaying toward zero. This feature reveals contributions beyond the leading-order hydrodynamic description.
authors: Ma\"elle Olivier, Filiberto Ares, Pasquale Calabrese

papers.title: Quantum kernels on breast data: concentration, surrogates, and two ways an advantage gets manufactured
papers.abstract: Quantum-kernel advantage claims on breast data are usually a single number: one quantum arm, one comparator, one test split. We asked what that number measures once the full comparator set and selection history are visible. We report three active benchmarks, all exact classical statevector simulations of 8-qubit fidelity kernels with no quantum component in the inference path: a sample-efficiency sweep on Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer at ten training-set sizes; raw-versus-processed arms on 1,200 M-SYNTH simulated mammograms with a matched closed-form dequantisation surrogate, five classical methods at the same input and eleven kernel families; and a 30-seed selection-inflation measurement on BreastMNIST. A CMMD D1 clinical arm is withdrawn as a result arm because its frozen splits leak the label through patient serial order, a defect reported in a separate study; it is retained only as a worked example. All three active arms are negative. On M-SYNTH raw an apparent +0.1736 (p = 5.2e-06) against a tuned RBF-SVM falls to +0.0019 (p = 0.937) against a random forest at the same input, and a Laplacian kernel wins on validation. On WDBC, with model selection confined to training data, the quantum kernel is below the selected classical arm at every training-set size, with 2 of 200 paired subsamples ahead. Best-of-30 seed selection adds +0.0210 on BreastMNIST. One result does not fit: at bandwidth 2pi the matched closed-form Gaussian surrogate failed to reproduce the M-SYNTH raw kernel (0.5410 against 0.7045, p = 6.3e-06). Comparator choice and selection each produce effects larger than any quantum-classical difference we measured; we give a reporting standard that removes both.
authors: Rana Saad, Achraf Toufah, Moulay Youssef El Hafidi

papers.title: Anomalous front propagation in many-body quantum transport with memory-dependent resetting
papers.abstract: We introduce an exactly solvable framework for non-Markovian quantum many-body dynamics based on stochastic resetting with memory. Applicable to arbitrary time-independent Hamiltonians, including interacting systems, our framework provides an exact representation of the dynamics with memory in terms of the corresponding reset-free evolution, which can be accessed either analytically or numerically. We demonstrate the power of this approach by studying domain-wall melting in a one-dimensional chain of noninteracting fermions, obtaining exact analytical results for the density profile, the local structure of the front edge, the extreme-value statistics of the rightmost fermion, and the integrated current. Remarkably, memory transforms ballistic transport into logarithmically slow propagation without arresting spreading. While the macroscopic density profile retains its original scaling function, the front edge broadens as $\sqrt{\ln t}$ rather than $t^{1/3}$ at late times and develops a qualitatively different edge structure. Furthermore, the extreme-value statistics change from Tracy--Widom to Gaussian, while both the mean and variance of the integrated current grow logarithmically in time. Our predictions are in excellent agreement with numerical simulations. These results reveal how memory can fundamentally alter quantum many-body transport and its fluctuations.
authors: Gabriele de Mauro, Manas Kulkarni, Satya N. Majumdar

papers.title: Quantum-Inspired Tensor Train Spectral Solver for High-Resolution PDEs with Non-Periodic Boundary Conditions
papers.abstract: Tensor train (TT) methods enable high-resolution computational mechanics simulations by exploiting low-rank structure in discretized fields and operators. While the superfast Fourier transform (SFFT) has enabled efficient TT-based spectral solvers for periodic problems, corresponding representations for non-periodic boundary conditions remain underexplored. We introduce the superfast cosine and sine transforms (SFCT and SFST), extending the TT spectral framework to homogeneous Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions, respectively. Building on a quantum-circuit construction of the discrete cosine and sine transforms, we derive both transforms from a shared TT operator representation and prove that their TT ranks are bounded by $6r_S$, independently of the discretization order, where $r_S$ is the rank of the SFFT at the prescribed accuracy. The measured ranks plateau near 32 for grid sizes up to $2^{26}$ points. For Rayleigh-B\'enard convection, spectral pressure projection achieves up to a 7-fold speedup in the Poisson solve relative to a preconditioned physical-space TT solver while maintaining comparable accuracy. Three-dimensional computational homogenization achieves a 2-6-fold speedup and a 4-7-fold reduction in memory consumption compared with the existing TT-based approach. The results establish an efficient TT framework for spectral PDE solvers with non-periodic boundary conditions.
authors: Sascha H. Hauck, Nis-Luca van H\"ulst, Matthias Kabel, Dieter Jaksch, Nicolas R. Gauger

papers.title: Confinement-induced Transitions of Chiral Active Particles and Dumbbells
papers.abstract: We present a coherent framework for the stochastic description of a chiral Active Brownian Particle (cABP) and a chiral Active Brownian Dumbbell (cABD) in a harmonic trap. On the one hand, we employ the Martin-Siggia-Rose path integral formalism, using the passive Brownian motion as a reference state around which activity is accounted for as a perturbation series in the self-propulsion speed. This method is suited best to calculate the exact time-dependent correlation functions. On the other hand, we use the Fokker-Planck equation, which works best to obtain the steady-state probability distribution. We discuss in detail the transitions from a trap centered distribution for low activity/strong confinement to a ring-shaped distribution for high activity/low confinement and the effect of chirality, i.e. the active angular velocity. For the dumbbell, a series of such transitions occurs and the correlation functions yield information about the particle's conformation and orientation. This establishes the combined framework as a powerful tool to investigate stochastic active particle systems.
authors: Mike Brandt, Falko Ziebert, Carsten Littek

papers.title: Local Thermodynamic Reconstruction of Impurity Entropy
papers.abstract: Resolving the thermodynamic entropy associated with a local impurity in a spatially extended interacting quantum bath remains a numerical challenge. We develop a Local-Maxwell approach that reconstructs the impurity entropy from local observables in worldline quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations. By integrating their temperature responses along the impurity coupling, the method avoids separate estimates of extensive entropies. For nonnegative worldline expansions with bounded local couplings, we establish bath-size independent bounds on all factorial moments of the impurity vertex count. For even vertex counts, the Maxwell estimator variance remains bounded as the coupling approaches zero. The transverse-field Ising benchmark reproduces exact free fermion results, while an interacting XXZ chain demonstrates up to several hundredfold improvement in statistical efficiency over conventional extensive thermodynamic integration. In a three-channel XXZ impurity junction, we reveal entropy recovery upon cooling and a nonmonotonic coupling dependence of the finite-temperature entropy contrast. These results establish local thermodynamic reconstruction as an efficient approach to impurity entropy in interacting quantum baths.
authors: Hang Su

papers.title: A lower bound on the Nusselt number in stochastically forced Rayleigh--B\'enard convection
papers.abstract: We establish a lower bound on the expected long-time averaged Nusselt number for two-dimensional Rayleigh--B\'enard convection at infinite Prandtl number, with free-slip boundaries and a suitable additive noise of amplitude $0<\sigma\leq1$ in the temperature equation. For every deterministic initial temperature, we prove that \[ \underline{Nu}-1 \geq c(\sigma^3 Ra)^{7/192}, \] provided that \[ \sigma^3 Ra \geq C(1+\log(1/\sigma))^{192/7}, \] where $c,C>0$ depend only on the domain parameter $L$. Without noise, no such bound can hold, since the conductive state is a solution with $Nu=1$ for every Rayleigh number. The proof uses the auxiliary functional method. For general Markov processes, we show that the defining inequality of an auxiliary functional need only hold after a short time average. This reduces the problem to showing that, with uniformly positive probability, the solution quickly leaves the set of states with low heat flux and low thermal dissipation. We establish this by projecting onto an unstable eigenvector of the linearization around the initial mean temperature profile, yielding a one-dimensional It\^o process with linear growth, additive noise, and nonlinear error terms.
authors: Juraj Foldes, Jun Hyun Park

papers.title: The Cosmological Constant as a Clock and the Vilenkin Wavefunction as a Resonance
papers.abstract: We address the problem of time in quantum gravity using a covariant formulation of unimodular gravity. As a result, the cosmological constant is canonically conjugate to a global four-volume variable, which serves as a clock and leads to a time-dependent Wheeler--DeWitt equation. We construct exact, background-independent solutions related to the full Chern--Simons--Kodama state and demonstrate unitary evolution in minisuperspace. The Chern--Simons functional also provides an intrinsic gravitational clock. These solutions reveal that the Vilenkin wavefunction is a gravitational Gamow resonance, in which its non-normalizability follows from the outgoing boundary condition. The tunneling probability into the expanding branch increases with the positive cosmological constant. These results give a dynamical interpretation of the wavefunction of the universe and clarify the role of its boundary conditions.
authors: Stephon Alexander, Marcell Howard

papers.title: Energy transport from an active medium
papers.abstract: We study the energy current through a harmonic chain whose left end is coupled, via a short-range contact potential, to a medium of overdamped run-and-tumble particles moving on a ring, while the right end is attached to a zero-temperature Langevin reservoir. The activity is parametrized by the propulsion speed $v_0$ and the persistence time $\tau$. Using nonequilibrium response theory at weak system-medium coupling, we predict the stationary current and simulations reproduce it over a large part of the $(v_0,\tau)$ plane. That includes the possible nonmonotonicity of the current as function of $v_0$ and $\tau$, and occurrence of resonances with the normal modes of the chain, most significantly at large $\tau$ and small $v_0$. There is a critical propulsion speed $v_c$ at which the ring-crossing frequency of the particles leaves the phonon band: for $v_0<v_c$ the current grows with persistence, while for $v_0>v_c$ it decays as $(v_0^2\tau)^{-1}$. We also explain where the theoretical prediction fails, especially due to an oscillatory instability originating from a sufficiently strong negative friction induced on the leftmost oscillator. Finally, the persistent medium produces strongly non-Gaussian velocity statistics and long-range, oscillating velocity correlations in the bulk of the chain.
authors: Simon Krekels, Christian Maes, Ion Santra

papers.title: Iterative Petz Protocols for Quantum State Recovery
papers.abstract: Noise is omnipresent in quantum systems, and thus, approximately reversing this noise is a central challenge towards quantum technologies. The Petz map provides a physically admissible recovery channel, but its performance depends critically on the choice of reference state. Here, we introduce and investigate the iterative Petz recovery (IPR) protocol, an adaptive multicopy strategy that begins from an unbiased reference state and uses each recovered output to construct the Petz map for the next iteration. We establish the stability of the protocol and develop a tomography-assisted finite-copy implementation with explicit control of error propagation and fidelity loss. For qubit depolarizing noise, we derive an exact recurrence for the fidelity of every pure input. For single-axis Pauli noise, we derive an exact recurrence for the six-state Pauli average and compare it numerically with the Haar average. We further benchmark finite-copy IPR against measure-and-prepare strategies based on local and collective measurements, revealing the associated finite-resource tradeoffs.
authors: Lea Lautenbacher, Felix Ahnefeld, Susana F. Huelga, Martin B. Plenio

papers.title: Polar Streams through Active Condensation in Flocks
papers.abstract: Two of the most paradigmatic phenomena in active matter are flocking, where particles align to move collectively, and motility-induced phase separation, where self-propulsion causes particles to condense even without attractive interactions. Here, using experiments on self-propelled Janus colloid dimers, we show that flocks can phase separate to form polar streams. These structures are elongated dense clusters of particles that flock along the stream's long axis, in contrast to the well-known transverse bands that form close to the flocking transition. We use particle-based simulations and hydrodynamic theory obtained through coarse-graining to identify the underlying mechanism, which we call active nematic condensation: Denser regions of the flock develop stronger polar and hence nematic order, which leads to further particle fluxes into the dense region. These results reveal a generic mechanism whereby flocks can condense into streams. Our findings uncover that flocks can be shaped by nematic order, which is usually not accounted for in the standard Toner-Tu equations. More broadly, our work shows that collective motion and phase separation can not only coexist but also cooperate in active matter.
authors: Lauritz Hahn, Xinyu Dou, Ziqi Zhou, Jie Zhang, Marin Bukov, Ricard Alert

papers.title: Z-Boson Production in Proton-Lead Collisions with MRW Nuclear TMDs
papers.abstract: The production of dileptons in proton-lead collisions probes the transverse-momentum structure of partons in a nuclear environment. We summarize a $k_t$-factorization study of $Z$ boson production at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=8.16\,\mathrm{TeV}$, comparing transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) distributions constructed with leading-order and Next-to-leading-order Martin-Ryskin-Watt (LO-MRW and NLO-MRW) prescriptions. Parton-level predictions obtained with \textsc{KaTie} are confronted with the CMS measurements in two invariant-mass regions, using the dilepton transverse momentum, $\phi^*_\eta$ and center-of-mass rapidity. The models describe the overall trends near the $Z$ resonance, while the virtuality constraint in NLO-MRW changes the high-transverse-momentum behavior. At lower dilepton masses, both prescriptions underestimate parts of the data, particularly the NLO-MRW result. These comparisons illustrate both the potential and the limitations of last-step-evolution nuclear TMD models for $Z$ boson production in proton-nucleus collisions.
authors: S. Rezaie, K. Azizi

papers.title: Polynomial Master Equations of Open Quantum Systems and an Analysis on the Critical Solutions
papers.abstract: The dynamics of open quantum systems exhibits in general a non-Markovian behavior, lying typically beyond the description of first-order differential equations. Traditional methods commonly turned to first-order integro-differential equations, which allowed for the standard interpretation of non-Markovianity as having its origin in the global history of the system evolution. We examine the possibility of an alternative, locally deterministic interpretation [arXiv:2607.09651] of the working of its dynamical hysteresis, where the evolution of a system is determined by its local behavior alone. The present work elaborates on our systematic method in deriving non-Markovian linear differential equations associated with matrix polynomials of higher order. Our methods will be demonstrated with exact analyses on two illustrative examples: one built upon the simplest non-trivial model concerning a two-qubit system, and another involving an unbounded Hamiltonian defined on an infinite-dimensional quantum system. We also analyze the critical parameters at which qualitative changes are observed in the system dynamics, and reveal how our polynomial equations account for the phenomena.
authors: Miku Ishizaki, Jaeha Lee

papers.title: Scalar-tensor interactions selected through their first-order thermodynamic dynamics
papers.abstract: We investigate the restrictive capability of first-order thermodynamics on scalar-tensor gravity. Starting from a general action containing nonlinear curvature dependence, an Einstein-tensor-Hessian coupling, and independent quadratic and cubic scalar-Hessian interactions, we derive the complete effective-fluid quantities. Simultaneously imposing Eckart's heat-conduction and shear-viscosity equations, while accounting for cancellations between interactions, substantially reduces the original operator basis and determines the geometric shear viscosity. Retaining the complete heat-conduction law, we establish an integrability condition that constrains the nonlinear Hessian interactions without prescribing the temperature and thermal conductivity. We construct explicit constitutive pairs and derive the associated thermal evolution, revealing contributions beyond the usual acceleration-aligned description. Remarkably, the thermodynamic integrability condition simplifies the scalar-metric kinetic structure such that imposing covariant degeneracy excludes the remaining nonlinear interactions, recovering the established luminal Horndeski subclass. Nonlinear thermodynamically compatible interactions nevertheless survive when degeneracy is restricted to the scalar-unitary gauge. These results establish a connection between thermodynamic integrability and dynamical degeneracy, demonstrating the potential of first-order thermodynamics as an independent and complementary criterion for selecting gravitational interactions.
authors: David S. Pereira

papers.title: Class-resolved sifting for quantum key distribution with photon pairs hyperentangled in polarization and transverse spatial variables
papers.abstract: Photon pairs hyperentangled in polarization and transverse spatial variables can carry two key bits per pair in entanglement-based quantum key distribution. We develop class-resolved sifting for such sources: every detected pair is assigned to a class according to which degrees of freedom were measured in compatible bases, and error and key rates are estimated separately in each class. Applied to previously reported data from a two-crystal spontaneous parametric down-conversion source read out in intermediate fractional-Fourier planes, the method recovers the key yield of independent sifting and turns the comparison between classes into a quantitative consistency test for cross-dependencies between the two degrees of freedom. The measured dependence lies below the spatial-polarization coupling predicted for the source, at the edge of the present statistical sensitivity. Resolving the data by polarization-analyzer setting, we find an approximately twofold dependence of the spatial error on the polarization setting in one readout arm, attributable to the measurement apparatus rather than to the source and relevant to basis-dependent side channels. We compare the hyperentangled protocol with a single 4-dimensional system measured in two mutually unbiased bases. Fundamentally, both yield the same key per detected pair and obey the same entropic bound, but they differ in their tensor-product structure: hyperentanglement factors the bases into separate two-outcome measurements, which are simpler to implement and allow errors to be attributed to each degree of freedom, whereas a single variable gives access to non-product bases that can increase the noise tolerance. For the present source, whose polarization coherence is limited by partial which-crystal erasure, a single-variable spatial encoding would yield more key only if its four-outcome readout kept the symbol error within a few percent.
authors: Murilo H. Magiotto, Millena B. Novaes, Wesley B. Cardoso, Ardiley T. Avelar, Guilherme L. Zanin, Rafael M. Gomes

papers.title: Finite-Temperature Superradiant Criticality and Thermal Emission in the Open Dicke Model
papers.abstract: Near the superradiant phase transition of the Dicke model, the lowest-frequency excitation softens and its losses can no longer be treated as a weak perturbation. We develop a finite-temperature theory of this transition in the open system, with no restriction on the strength of the system-bath coupling. The cavity mode and the atomic ensemble are coupled to independent reservoirs, the first at zero temperature and the second at temperature $T$, and we assume that the spins remain thermalized with their reservoir. We find that the reservoirs do not shift the temperature-dependent critical coupling for a broad class of spectral densities, while the polariton becomes overdamped in a finite interval of couplings around it. As expected, raising the temperature moves the transition to stronger couplings, and in the superradiant phase we find a faster decoupling of light and matter. The theoretical framework developed here yields the reflection and thermal emission spectra for arbitrary parameters in both the normal and the superradiant phase, and provides a basis for comparison with experiments on systems displaying ground-state condensation. We also identify conditions under which the system behaves, at specific frequencies, as both a perfect absorber and a perfect emitter.
authors: Gabriele Orlando, Samuel Napoli, Salvatore Savasta, Omar Di Stefano

papers.title: Holographic ensembles and giant gravitons at the Leigh--Strassler fixed point
papers.abstract: Finite-rank observables in holographic quantum field theories provide stringent tests of string and M-theory, but remain challenging to compute when supersymmetry is non-maximal. In this paper, we study the finite rank partition function of the $\mathcal N=1$ Leigh-Strassler CFT, which admits an interacting Fermi-gas description. We compute the partition function explicitly in two ensembles: the canonical ensemble at fixed rank $N$, and the grand canonical ensemble, where $N$ is summed over while its conjugate chemical potential $\mu$ is held fixed. In line with recent proposals, we find that the perturbative large-$N$ and large-$\mu$ expansions in both ensembles are reproduced by the on-shell action and one-loop determinant over Kaluza--Klein modes of type IIB supergravity, with appropriate ensemble-dependent boundary terms. Furthermore, the one-loop partition function of a D3-brane giant graviton precisely matches the leading nonperturbative correction to the boundary partition functions.
authors: Jesse van Muiden, De-liang Zhong

papers.title: Bound-state preparation in strongly coupled theories
papers.abstract: Many quantum simulation tasks, including scattering in quantum field theories and effective non-relativistic theories, require the preparation of asymptotic states. Such a state, which may be a bound state, is typically the lowest-lying excited state in some sector of Hilbert space. At weak coupling these states can often be prepared adiabatically by beginning with the free theory, but this is not generally feasible in strongly coupled theories. We detail a family of algorithms for preparing composite states in strongly coupled theories, including non-Abelian gauge theories, by using weakly coupled auxiliary fields. These methods do not require quantum phase estimation. We demonstrate the method numerically, via classical simulation, on nonrelativistic theories in one spatial dimension. We estimate the yield of this method applied to $J/\psi$ production in quantum chromodynamics.
authors: Scott Lawrence, Duff Neill

papers.title: A model colloidal gel former for the measurement of inter-particle forces
papers.abstract: Tracking of particle coordinates in colloidal model systems is an established technique. Recently, an emulsion system has been introduced where not only the coordinates, but also contacts and compressive forces between the droplets can be determined [Dong et al. J. Chem. Phys. 156 214907 (2022). Here we develop this system to control both the density mismatch and refractive index contrast between the emulsion droplets and the solvent. The former is important in minimizing sedimentation due to gravity and the latter is necessary for 3d imaging with confocal microscopy. By mapping our system carefully to computer simulation, we quantify interdroplet forces and packing geometries in depletion gels and probe the relationship between local structure and compressive stress. The simulations also provide ensemble measurements of the attractive part of the force between droplets and related quantities such as the stress tensor. Finally, we implement an improved measure of local stress in our experiments, which can be directly compared with the corresponding quantity in simulations. We find that locally rigid minimum energy clusters are associated with regions of higher stress in the gel network.
authors: Rui Cheng, Kristian Thijssen, Abraham Mauleon Amieva, Tanniemola B. Liverpool, Malcolm A. Faers, Robert L. Jack, C. Patrick Royall

papers.title: CANON: Agent-Assisted Construction of Canonical Differential Equations for Feynman Integrals
papers.abstract: The construction of canonical basis is an important procedure in the calculation of multi-loop Feynman integrals via the canonical differential equation methods. Currently, there are various different methods for this purpose. Among them, no single method is universally applicable. Thus, obtaining a valid basis often requires repeated attempts and verification. In this paper, we present CANON, an agent-assisted framework designed to make this search-and-verification process more convenient and more efficient. In this workflow, the agent selects methods and calls the corresponding tools to revise the basis proposal or the associated differential-equation system. Independent programs then verify whether the agent's result is valid and ask the agent to retry if verification fails. This framework contains a specific state-management tool to supports long-range basis searching works which requires multiple sub-agents. Its modular architecture enables future extensions to the framework itself. In this paper, we demonstrate this framework by applying it to some two-loop and three-loop integral families.
authors: Dong-shan Jian, Yuanche Liu, Yan-qing Ma, Bo-xuan Shi, Yu Wu, Zihao Wu, Yang Zhang

papers.title: Robust growth of $\alpha$-tantalum on sapphire at room temperature using atomically thin titanium seed layer
papers.abstract: Tantalum (Ta) based superconducting circuits have attracted attention for their low microwave loss. However, reproducible growth of high-quality $\alpha$-phase Ta films remains challenging because film properties are highly sensitive to growth conditions. We present a robust, room-temperature route for $\alpha$-Ta growth on sapphire substrates using an ultrathin Ti seed layer, which significantly widens the accessible deposition parameter space. We compare this approach to Ta films grown at high temperature without a seed layer and at room temperature with a Nb seed. We assess films using structural and surface characterization and quantify microwave loss with coplanar-waveguide (CPW) resonators measured in the quantum regime. We obtain two-level-system (TLS)-limited quality factors comparable to the state of the art for Ta-on-sapphire CPW resonators with similar geometries. In addition, temperature-dependent measurements reveal that high-temperature-grown films and films subjected to extended buffered-oxide etch treatment exhibit additional temperature activated loss, highlighting the role of growth route and post-processing in microwave performance. Our results establish ultrathin seed-layer engineering as a reliable alternative route to reproducible, low-loss $\alpha$-Ta films and motivate closer study of the interfacial mechanisms that govern Ta phase formation.
authors: Anand Kamlapure, Lucas Hak, Kishore Kumar Thiyagarajan, Hozanna Miro, Marc Beekman, Matvey Finkel, Leonardo DiCarlo

papers.title: Anomalies and the Berry Phase: From $\pi^0\to\gamma\gamma$ to the geometry of the fermion vacuum
papers.abstract: We review the chiral anomaly from a historical perspective, from the $\pi^0\to\gamma\gamma$ puzzle and the work of Adler, Bell and Jackiw, to the Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) term. We then describe how the WZW term was motivated from quantum chromodynamics in 1983-85. Integrating out the non-Abelian gauge fields, that have a gapped spectrum, gives a Nambu-Jona-Lasinio type theory of quarks, and integrating out the quarks, which are gapped by chiral symmetry breaking, gives the WZW model. The fermion determinant splits into a regulator-dependent modulus, which gives the dynamics of mesons, and a universal phase, which is fixed by the anomaly and is the WZW term. Restricted to the collective coordinates of the baryon soliton, the WZW term imposes a U(1) constraint that makes the baryon wave functions monopole harmonics and fixes their spin, statistics and flavour multiplets. We then explain that this phase is a Berry phase: the Schwinger terms of current algebra are the curvature of a U(1) connection on the space of chiral field configurations, and the WZW term is its holonomy, which we call a Berry-Wilson loop. In 1+1 dimensions we write the connection explicitly in terms of Euler angles, exhibiting a Dirac monopole whose quantised charge is the level of the current algebra.
authors: Spenta R. Wadia

papers.title: Scalar perturbations in extremal Reissner-Nordstr\"om geometry: new methods at work
papers.abstract: We study scalar radiation emitted by a particle moving along a circular orbit around a four-dimensional extremal Reissner-Nordstr\"om black hole. In particular, we calculate the energy fluxes carried by scalar waves to infinity and across the event horizon, as well as the scalar self-force acting on the particle, and express all these quantities as post-Newtonian expansions. Our results for the energy fluxes are in agreement with previous numerical findings in the literature. To solve the radial wave equation, we employ and test two distinct analytic approaches: the first is the so-called \textit{kink method}, a novel alternative stemming from quantum integrability and the second is the Mano-Suzuki-Takasugi method. The perfect agreement of the results highlights the potential of the kink method as a complementary tool for studying wave propagation in black-hole spacetimes.
authors: Giorgio Di Russo, Davide Fioravanti, Francesco Olivi, Marco Rossi

papers.title: Non-formality of prefactorization algebras
papers.abstract: We construct a Poisson bracket on the cohomology of locally constant prefactorization algebras on $\mathbb{R}^m$ that provides an obstruction to formality in every dimension $m\geqslant 2$. Our construction combines colored obstruction sequences to formality with linking spheres and generalizes the two-dimensional bracket of Bruinsma, Schenkel, and Vicedo. We use it to extend their non-formality theorem for Lie algebra factorization envelopes to all higher dimensions. We also establish new non-formality results for factorization envelopes of Lie algebras, their compactifications and generalizations to $L_\infty$-algebras, free BF-type theories, higher abelian Chern-Simons theories and their compactifications.
authors: Coline Emprin, Alex Takeda

papers.title: Classical algorithms for sparse random Hamiltonians via free probability
papers.abstract: The search for quantum advantage in average-case problems is a pressing open question in physics and computer science. The widest conjectured example of such an advantage is in simulation of quantum many-body systems, where sign problems and entanglement growth cause the breakdown of many classical methods. Nonetheless, theoretical evidence for or against such an advantage remains scarce. Here, we investigate this in sparse random non-local Hamiltonians. We design a classical algorithm for such Hamiltonians that enables accurate computation of spectral fluctuations, thermal values, and time-ordered and out-of-time-order correlation functions. For any subexponential precision $\varepsilon$, our algorithm runs in time $(1/\varepsilon)^{2+o(1)}$, nearly identical to a quantum simulation. Crucially, this applies even at late evolution times, low temperatures, and near critical points, where existing classical methods require exponential time. Rather than directly simulating a quantum state or operator, our algorithm first computes the model's mean behavior and then a short hierarchy of instance-dependent corrections. These corrections predict long-time behavior based on short-time data using free probability theory.
authors: Matthew Ding, Robbie King, Thomas Schuster

papers.title: A Koashi--Imoto Criterion for Holevo-Rate Visible Compression
papers.abstract: For a finite memoryless quantum source whose encoder knows the sequence of classical labels, we determine when the Holevo rate is achievable with shared classical randomness and no shared entanglement. In the maximal Koashi--Imoto decomposition of the signal ensemble, this occurs exactly when each signal is pure on the quantum part of every sector it occupies. For qubits, this means that the signals are all pure or commute pairwise. If any occupied quantum part is mixed, every code with sufficiently small mean local error has rate bounded away from the Holevo information, uniformly in blocklength. To prove the converse, we apply Fawzi--Renner recovery to a hypothetical sequence of visible codes approaching the Holevo rate at vanishing local error, then invoke a decoupling bound of Baghali Khanian and Winter for blind compression.
authors: Anthony M. Polloreno

papers.title: Energy and topology of Ricci-flat 4-manifolds
papers.abstract: We show that there is $C>0$ such that any complete Ricci-flat $4$-manifold $(M,g)$ satisfies $$ b_2(M)-C\leqslant\frac1{8\pi^2}\int_M|R_g|_g^2\,dv_g\leqslant b_2(M)+C, $$ where $R$ is the curvature operator. No assumption is made on volume growth, model at infinity or curvature decay. It follows that uncountably many exotic $\mathbb R^4$ admit no complete Ricci-flat metric, and that complete noncompact hyperk\"ahler metrics with finite $b_2$ have ends classified by Sun-Zhang. This also provides information about the thin part of immortal four-dimensional Ricci flows in Bamler's decomposition. The proof refines the chopping method of Cheeger-Gromov and Cheeger-Tian by bounding the topology of boundaries of regions exhausting the manifold.
authors: Tristan Ozuch

papers.title: Prospects and limitations of adaptive variational quantum algorithms for lattice field theories: a case study in 2+1 dimensions
papers.abstract: The variational quantum algorithm ADAPT-VQE has previously been used to prepare the vacuum of lattice gauge theories in $1+1D$. In this paper, we study whether it extends to higher dimensions. We identify two general limitations of ADAPT-VQE. First, if the qubit Hamiltonian and the initial state are real, i.e., invariant under qubit-level time-reversal, all real-valued pool operators have vanishing gradients and are never selected. Second, the algorithm can converge to excited eigenstates. We illustrate both limitations, also providing examples from literature, and present a first application of ADAPT-VQE to a lattice field theory in $2+1D$, namely free Wilson fermions, where both obstacles occur. Adding charge conjugation symmetry to the operator pool improves the results, and combining different pools with suitable initial states recovers the ground and first excited states over the full mass range. These findings give practical guidelines for applying ADAPT-VQE to lattice field theories beyond $1+1D$.
authors: Nico Dichter, Andrea Bulgarelli, Lena Funcke, Stefan K\"{u}hn

papers.title: $QQ\bar Q\bar Q$ Quark System and Gauge/String Duality II: String Breaking
papers.abstract: This is the second of two companion papers in which we continue developing the construction of the fully heavy tetraquark system using the gauge/string duality. Here, we extend this construction to model $SU(3)$ gauge theory with two light flavors of equal mass. As an application, we analyze the two lowest Born-Oppenheimer potentials, both analytically and numerically, for rectangular and collinear geometries. Our analysis reveals several critical scales associated with string reconnection and breaking, as well as junction annihilation and pinching. In addition, we find that the string tension is universal, whereas the string breaking distance is not.
authors: Oleg Andreev

papers.title: The double copy and perturbative teleparallel gravity
papers.abstract: In this paper we analyze the double copy between gluon and graviton amplitudes within the context of teleparallel gravity. We first set up an effective Lagrangian based on minimal assumptions which reproduces the on-shell amplitudes stemming from the double-copy procedure. By straightforwardly computing the three- and four-point amplitude, this double-copy Lagrangian can be constrained up to a few real parameters when expanding to quartic order. For a specific choice of parameters, we find an exact equivalence with perturbative teleparallel gravity. This suggests that the teleparallel formulation might be well suited to make the double copy more transparent from a Lagrangian viewpoint.
authors: Georg Stettinger

papers.title: Topological insulators on site-eliminated, projected, and patterned fractal lattices
papers.abstract: Identifying fractal lattices of fractional (Hausdorff) dimension as geometric descendants of parent crystals, we showcase the successful realization of canonical topological insulators in one-, two-, and three-dimensional crystals on their self-similar descents using three complementary approaches, starting from lattice-regularized models in integer dimensions. (a) In the first approach, we construct the fractal Hamiltonian by removing all parent-lattice sites that do not belong to such a network (method of site elimination). (b) In the second one, we integrate or project out the same set of sites to obtain an effective Hamiltonian for the fractal lattice (method of projection or renormalization). (c) In the third approach, we retain the parent-crystal lattice intact but spatially pattern the on-site mass parameter, which controls the topology of the parent insulating system, such that it assumes two topologically distinct values on the fractal network and its complement (patterned fractal lattices). By numerically diagonalizing the resulting Hamiltonians and computing appropriate topological invariants or local markers, corroborating the bulk-boundary correspondence through gapless modes at outer or inner boundaries, we establish Su-Schrieffer-Heeger topology on the Cantor set using all three approaches, Haldane topology on the hexaflake [using (a) and (b)] and Qi-Wu-Zhang topology on the Sierpi\'nski carpet [using (c)], and strong $Z_2$ topological insulating phases on the tiled Menger sponge from methods (a), (b), and (c). These findings complement and substantially extend the previously reported realization of Qi-Wu-Zhang topology on the Sierpi\'nski carpet using methods (a) and (b) [Phys. Rev. B 110, L241302 (2024)].
authors: Aiden Mains, Danile Salib, Christopher Leong, Bitan Roy
